title: Procurement Coordinator
description:
About Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About Role

We’re looking for a Procurement Coordinator to support the day-to-day purchasing and logistics needs of our Robotics organization. You’ll follow up on orders, coordinate domestic and international shipments, work with suppliers and logistics providers, and keep the details organized from purchase request through delivery.

This is an entry-level position for someone who is organized, curious, and eager to take ownership. You don’t need years of procurement experience, but you should be comfortable asking questions, learning quickly, and following through. When an email goes unanswered, you pick up the phone. When a delivery is at risk, you find out why, identify the next step, and keep the right people informed.

You’ll also help improve how we work. We expect you to adopt AI tools and build practical automations that reduce repetitive tasks, improve visibility, and make the supply chain team more effective. This role offers an opportunity to build a foundation in procurement, logistics, and hardware operations.



This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week and up to 10% travel to vendor sites.

In this role you will:

 - Follow up with internal teams to keep purchase requests and PO issuance moving on time, resolve missing information, and confirm that suppliers receive and acknowledge orders.

 - Track open orders through delivery, maintain accurate supplier commitments, and proactively follow up on lead times, shipment dates, and overdue items.

 - Coordinate domestic and international logistics, including scheduling couriers, arranging pickups, booking shipments, tracking deliveries, and resolving shipping exceptions.

 - Prepare and check commercial invoices, packing lists, and other shipping documentation. Work with suppliers, customs brokers, and internal specialists to address customs questions and support timely clearance.

 - Manage day-to-day coordination with third-party logistics providers (3PLs), including receiving, storage, outbound shipments, and resolving inventory or delivery discrepancies.

 - Keep purchasing and logistics records current, communicate clear status updates, and help resolve order discrepancies, returns, and missing delivery documentation.

 - Use AI, spreadsheets, and workflow automation tools to streamline order tracking, follow-up reminders, shipment updates, and routine reporting. Check that the resulting information is accurate and useful.

 - Support the broader supply chain team as priorities shift. Take action on open issues, call suppliers when email isn’t working, and escalate risks early with clear context and proposed next steps.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are starting your career and want to build experience in procurement, logistics, or operations. Relevant experience can come from internships, school projects, part-time work, or other roles where you managed details and followed through.

 - Are highly organized and attentive to detail. You can keep track of multiple orders, deadlines, and follow-ups without losing sight of what matters most.

 - Have a bias for action. You’re comfortable contacting an unfamiliar supplier, asking direct questions, and following up persistently and professionally.

 - Communicate clearly and close the loop. People know what’s happening, what’s blocked, and what you’re doing next.

 - Are comfortable with spreadsheets and learning new systems. You actively experiment with AI tools and can turn a repetitive task into a more reliable workflow.

 - Adapt well to changing priorities, ask for help when needed, and exercise sound judgment about when to act independently and when to escalate.

 - Are curious about robotics, hardware, and how physical goods move through a supply chain. Prior exposure to purchasing systems, shipping, customs documentation, or warehouse operations is helpful but not required.

What success looks like:

Within the first 6 months, you will have:

 - Established reliable tracking for your assigned orders, with current commitments, clear next actions, and timely follow-up.

 - Built effective working relationships with suppliers, couriers, customs brokers, and 3PLs.

 - Become dependable at coordinating routine domestic and international shipments, preparing documentation, and escalating exceptions appropriately.

 - Earned the team’s trust through accurate records, responsive communication, and consistent follow-through.

title: Business Recruiter, APAC
description:
About this Team

At OpenAI, we’re here to do something extraordinary: build safe AGI that benefits everyone. That mission demands people who are not just brilliant but also deeply aligned with our values. Our Recruiting team is the gateway connecting exceptional humans to meaningful, high-impact work. We’re a close-knit, mission-driven crew that takes pride in thoughtful, relationship-first hiring. We partner deeply with teams across OpenAI to find, engage, and support the people who will shape the future of AI.

 

About this Role

We’re looking for an experienced Business Recruiter to help build some of the most critical teams at OpenAI, primarily focused on technical business roles within our B2B and go-to-market organisation. You’ll also need the versatility to take on hiring across other teams as business priorities evolve.

This is a high-impact role where you’ll operate as a strategic talent partner not just executing searches, but shaping how we attract, assess, and hire exceptional talent globally. You’ll own searches end-to-end, working closely with senior stakeholders to define hiring strategies, navigate complex markets, and deliver outstanding outcomes.

You’ll report to the APAC Recruiting Lead and collaborate closely with global recruiting, People, and business leadership to scale our organisation in a thoughtful, high-quality way.

Your responsibilities

 - Own end-to-end hiring for APAC roles, from scoping and calibration through to offer and close.

 - Partner closely with senior business leaders to deeply understand team needs, define hiring strategies, and translate business priorities into actionable talent plans.

 - Build and execute proactive, data-informed sourcing strategies to attract high-calibre and diverse talent across competitive markets.

 - Act as a trusted advisor to hiring managers, driving alignment, challenging assumptions, and maintaining a consistently high hiring bar.

 - Deliver an exceptional candidate experience, ensuring every interaction reflects OpenAI’s values and mission.

 - Navigate complex, global hiring environments by partnering with People, Legal, and Compensation to ensure consistency, fairness, and compliance.

 - Continuously improve recruiting processes, identifying bottlenecks and implementing scalable solutions to increase quality and velocity.

 - Bring market intelligence and insights to stakeholders, influencing hiring decisions and shaping talent strategy.

We’re seeking:

 - 7+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, ideally in-house at high-growth or high-bar environments.

 - Proven track record of hiring for business functions (e.g. Sales, Technical Success, RevOps, Partnerships, User Ops), preferably working on Technical roles. 

 - Strong talent judgment, you can assess both experience and potential, and consistently raise the bar.

 - Comfortable operating as a strategic partner, influencing senior stakeholders and navigating ambiguity.

 - Highly execution-oriented, with the ability to run multiple complex searches simultaneously without sacrificing quality.

 - Skilled in building pipelines from scratch, especially in competitive or emerging talent markets.

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Growth
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments and other OpenAI products worldwide. We work across the full funnel—from awareness and acquisition through activation, retention, and expansion—using experimentation, data science, machine learning, and product engineering to help more people discover and realize durable value from OpenAI’s products.

Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Finance, Lifecycle, and Growth Marketing. We move quickly, test rigorously, and hold a high bar for measurement, privacy, reliability, and user trust.




ABOUT THIS ROLE: 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to build the models and decision systems that optimize paid marketing investment for ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. You will develop budget allocation and control algorithms that determine where to invest, how quickly to spend, and how to adjust as performance changes.

The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build budget allocation algorithms. Decide how to distribute investment across channels, campaigns, and markets using estimates of marginal returns, while accounting for diminishing returns, uncertainty, and business constraints.

 - Develop spend pacing and adaptive control systems. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior.

 - Model marketing response and user value. Develop forecasts and models of conversion, long-term value, and saturation that help determine where the next dollar can have the greatest impact.

 - Evaluate decisions rigorously. Use simulations, backtesting, and online experiments to test allocation and control policies. Partner with Data Science to measure incrementality and validate whether offline improvements translate into better investment outcomes.

 - Own reliable production systems. Build data pipelines, training and inference workflows, and integrations that turn model outputs into budget decisions. Establish data-quality checks, monitoring, and retraining with thoughtful treatment of privacy and consent.

 - Turn business goals into optimization problems. Partner with Growth Marketing, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance to define objectives and constraints, communicate tradeoffs, and use evidence to improve investment decisions.

 - Help build a diverse and inclusive culture where people feel welcome, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with candor and respect.




You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist, Data Scientist, or in a comparable quantitative engineering role, or an equivalent record of impact.

 - Experience building and operating production ML or quantitative decision systems, from problem formulation and data pipelines through deployment, experimentation, and monitoring.

 - Strong software engineering skills, proficiency in Python and SQL, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks and large-scale data systems.

 - Strong foundations in machine learning and statistics, with experience applying optimization or control methods to decisions under uncertainty.

 - Experience evaluating models or algorithms with noisy, delayed, or incomplete data, and the judgment to balance model quality, causal impact, and operational reliability.

 - The ability to turn ambiguous goals into focused experiments, interpret mixed results, and communicate clear decisions with technical and non-technical partners.

 - A collaborative working style and a commitment to deploying AI responsibly, in service of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

 - Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

title: Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices
description:
We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.



A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.



You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.



This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.



In This Role, You Will

 - Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

 - Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

 - Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

 - Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

 - Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

 - Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

 - Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

 - Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

 - Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

 - Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

 - Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

 - Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

 - Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

 - Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.



Minimum Qualifications

 - 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

 - Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.



You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

 - A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

 - Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

 - Experience developing one or more of the following:
   
   - HSM firmware or trusted applications
   
   - Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services
   
   - HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware
   
   - PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations
   
   - Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols
   
   - HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems
   
   - Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

 - Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

 - Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

 - Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.

 - Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.

 - The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.

 - Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.



Additional Experience That May Be Helpful

 - Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.

 - Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.

 - Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.

 - Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.

 - Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.

 - Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.

 - Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.

 - Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.

 - Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.

 - Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

description:
About the Team

Like every team at OpenAI, the Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. We develop strategies that drive awareness, engagement, and usage of OpenAI’s products and platform, helping people and businesses understand and realize the value of AI.

The Marketing Insights & Analytics team develops a deep understanding of markets, audiences, behaviors, attitudes, and needs to inform marketing, product, and business decisions. We partner across OpenAI to build foundational audience understanding, shape marketing strategy, inform thought leadership, and measure performance.

About the Role

As Market Research Lead, ChatGPT you will help shape our Insights & Analytics strategy and set research direction for a major business area or cross-functional initiative. As a senior individual contributor, you will independently define and lead multiple complex research workstreams, connecting audience behavior, perceptions, and feedback to decisions across product, brand, and growth.

You will anticipate emerging business questions, bring structure to ambiguous challenges, and translate research into recommendations that influence senior leadership. Alongside delivering hands-on research, you will establish methodological standards, develop foundational research frameworks, and mentor experienced peers.

In this role, you will:

 - Set research strategy, priorities, and goals for a major business area, aligning the research agenda with critical decisions and anticipating future needs.

 - Independently define, prioritize, and lead multiple complex quantitative and qualitative research workstreams, balancing business impact, rigor, speed, and resources.

 - Serve as a strategic partner to brand, product marketing, creative, product, and other teams, helping shape business strategy and goals through insights.

 - Address challenges such as reaching new audiences, evolving our brand, positioning our product suite, and improving experiences.

 - Connect primary research with behavioral data and other evidence, partnering with analytics colleagues to build a holistic understanding of our audiences.

 - Translate complex findings into clear narratives and actionable recommendations that influence senior leaders and align stakeholders around decisions.

 - Set technical and quality standards for research design, execution, analysis, and interpretation, including work delivered by agencies and vendors.

 - Develop reusable frameworks and foundational research that strengthen the team’s ability to answer complex questions over time.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 12+ years of experience in mixed-method market research and data analysis, with deep expertise in quantitative and qualitative methods.

 - A track record of setting research strategy and independently leading multiple complex workstreams across a substantial business area or cross-functional initiative.

 - Strong judgment in ambiguous situations, including identifying the right questions, prioritizing competing needs, and choosing methods that support consequential decisions.

 - Hands-on expertise across the full research lifecycle, including instrument design, sampling, weighting, statistical analysis, and reporting.

 - Demonstrated success synthesizing evidence from multiple sources into recommendations that influence senior leadership and marketing, product, or business strategy.

 - Experience spanning product or go-to-market research, positioning and messaging, brand strategy, campaign development, and tracking.

 - Experience conducting global research and managing agencies or vendors to deliver high-quality outcomes.

 - Experience establishing research standards, developing reusable frameworks, and mentoring experienced researchers or cross-functional peers.

 - Proficiency with statistical analysis and survey programming.

 - Excited to make AI part of how you work—actively experimenting with new tools and finding practical ways to improve the quality, speed, and impact of your work

title: Software Engineer, Cloud Computer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Browser Use team builds the technology that enables agents to interact with browsers across our products. Our work spans infrastructure, tooling, and user experiences, both on users’ devices and in the cloud. We partner with research to improve our models’ browser-use capabilities and with web standards bodies to shape how agents interact with the web. Our products include ChatGPT for Chrome, the ChatGPT in-app browser, and the cloud computer used in dots and ChatGPT Work.


We see the browser as a universal connector. If we can enable our models to use it effectively, they can do anything. Come help us build the future of browsing!




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a product-oriented engineer to build and scale our cloud computer infrastructure. Our goal is to give every one of our users access to an agent with their own computer in the cloud. Build novel solutions to problems like authentication, user takeover, and enterprise network access. You’ll help own the systems that provision, run, and manage the environments our agents use, making them reliable, responsive, and efficient as demand grows.


This role combines infrastructure depth with close attention to the user experience. You’ll partner with research and engineering teams to bring new computer-use capabilities into production, working across container orchestration, backend services, and product experiences.




IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Build and scale infrastructure for running agent-controlled browsers and computers in the cloud.

 - Develop services for provisioning environments, managing sessions, and coordinating their lifecycle.

 - Improve reliability, performance, resource utilization, and observability across the fleet.

 - Diagnose issues across Linux, containers, networking, and browser execution.

 - Build APIs and tooling that make cloud computers easy for research and product teams to use.

 - Work closely with research to understand emerging requirements and improve how computer use works.

 - Develop authentication, credential management, and network access controls that protect user data and support interactions with websites and services.




YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE

 - Experience leading large-scale backend, platform, or infrastructure projects from ambiguous problem statements to production systems.

 - Proficiency in one or more backend languages such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or similar, and the ability to move across service, platform, and product boundaries.

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems, cloud platforms, and production reliability.

 - Own systems from initial design through deployment and scale.

 - Comfort with a fast-moving pace while caring for security and operational excellence.

title: Strategic Delivery Lead, Critical Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The OpenAI for Government team is a mission-driven group bringing frontier AI to public-sector and national security missions. We partner with government agencies and their industry counterparts to apply OpenAI’s API and enterprise products to high-priority challenges, with careful attention to security, privacy, reliability, and responsible use.

In this role, you will help government agencies, infrastructure owners and operators, and technology partners apply frontier AI to strengthen critical infrastructure security and resilience. You will connect technical teams and mission leaders to develop practical applications for cyber defense and operational preparedness across sectors such as energy, water, healthcare, financial services, and the defense industrial base. We accelerate adoption through hands-on support, tailored enablement, and measurable outcomes while preserving human judgment and protecting sensitive information.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Strategic Delivery Lead (SDL) for Critical Infrastructure will identify, shape, and deliver OpenAI’s highest-impact engagements supporting the security and resilience of U.S. critical infrastructure. You will help government and industry partners translate priorities—including cyber defense, vulnerability management, incident preparedness and response, infrastructure risk analysis, and operational coordination—into secure, technically feasible AI deployments.

This role sits at the intersection of technical delivery, public-private collaboration, and national cyber strategy. You will work with federal agencies, infrastructure operators, and technology providers to define shared goals and turn promising pilots into sustainable operational capabilities. Internally, you will partner with Research, Engineering, Go-to-Market, Security, Legal, Privacy, and other teams to align scope, resolve delivery obstacles, and communicate progress from working teams to senior leadership.

You will own end-to-end execution of delivery workstreams with Forward Deployed Engineers, Researchers, Solutions Architects, and Enablement teams. You will establish outcomes, requirements, roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria; coordinate integration, evaluation, security review, and rollout; and remain accountable for contractual milestones, delivery governance, and measurable customer value.

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. Success requires technical fluency, strong program leadership, executive presence, and sound judgment about deploying AI in environments where service continuity and public trust matter.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build trusted relationships with government mission owners, cyber leaders, sector risk management agencies, infrastructure owners and operators, and technology partners to identify and prioritize high-value AI applications.

 - Own complex engagements from discovery and solution shaping through pilot, security review, deployment, customer acceptance, and sustained adoption. Establish delivery roadmaps, integrated schedules, risk tracking, decision processes, and customer reporting.

 - Translate critical infrastructure missions, cyber risks, policy requirements, data constraints, and operating conditions into clear technical requirements, delivery plans, and executive communications.

 - Develop public-private delivery efforts with federal cyber agencies, sector partners, cloud providers, and cybersecurity companies. Align organizations with different incentives, resources, and definitions of success around shared operational outcomes.

 - Lead delivery of AI capabilities supporting defensive workflows such as vulnerability discovery and prioritization, secure software development, threat analysis, incident response, and infrastructure risk assessment, partnering with technical and operational experts on design, evaluation, and execution.

 - Coordinate deployment requirements across government and enterprise environments, including sensitive or restricted networks where appropriate. Address data handling, identity and access controls, integration dependencies, and customer security requirements.

 - Work with security, privacy, legal, and operational stakeholders to establish evaluations, human oversight, adversarial testing, and ongoing monitoring appropriate to each use case, including potential effects on operational technology and essential services.

 - Define and track measures of customer value, including user adoption, model quality, operational readiness, time saved, and improvements in defensive effectiveness.

 - Bring insight from customers and partners back to Research, Product, and Engineering to inform capability development and deployment priorities. Anticipate technical, operational, contractual, and partnership risks and resolve delivery tradeoffs.

 - Support opportunity qualification, proposal development, and statements of work with Account Directors and partners. Define a practical path from pilot to sustained adoption, including operational ownership, resources, funding, and measures of success.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 10+ years of experience leading critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, national security, or complex technical programs, including substantial experience working with U.S. government agencies and industry partners.

 - Hold an active U.S. Government TS/SCI clearance and can meet customer-specific access requirements.

 - Are willing to travel up to 50% and work on-site with customers and partners to understand their missions, users, and operating environments.

 - Understand the U.S. critical infrastructure ecosystem, including federal cyber agencies, sector risk management agencies, infrastructure owners and operators, and the public-private partnerships that support national resilience.

 - Have led complex programs or public-private initiatives from strategy and planning through execution and sustained operations. Can translate policy objectives into technical work streams, clear ownership, and measurable results.

 - Bring executive presence and experience advising senior government, industry, and technical leaders. Can explain complex cyber and AI issues, address objections, and build agreement across organizations.

 - Have the technical fluency to work credibly with researchers, engineers, and cyber practitioners. Understand modern AI solution architectures—including large language models, enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, and data integration—and can work with technical teams to assess feasibility, evaluation needs, and delivery risks.

 - Can turn customer outcomes into requirements, statements of work, integrated schedules, acceptance criteria, and evaluation plans. Understand what makes a pilot operationally and financially sustainable.

 - Understand the security and reliability constraints of critical infrastructure, including the relationship between information technology, operational technology, and continuity of essential services.

 - Build durable partnerships across government, industry, research, and technical teams. Create clarity in ambiguous situations, adapt when evidence changes, and build trust through accountability, curiosity, and open communication.

 - Care deeply about strengthening national resilience and helping critical infrastructure partners use frontier AI safely, responsibly, and effectively.

title: Researcher, Safety - Frontier Assurance
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Frontier Assurance team strengthens OpenAI’s safety decisions through independent expertise, rigorous assessment, and public transparency. We coordinate external evaluations of frontier models and safeguards, develop approaches such as embedded auditing, and manage the misalignment disclosure process and safeguard testing. Our work helps independent experts scrutinize OpenAI’s safety approach and ensures their findings inform consequential decisions about advanced AI systems.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a researcher on Frontier Assurance, you will build the technical foundations for rigorous assessments of frontier AI risks. You will help design technical assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.

You will work closely with external evaluators and embedded auditors, helping them understand the systems they are assessing and access the models, data, and technical information their work requires. Where direct access is not possible, you will conduct experiments and analyses on their behalf, with methods and results they can meaningfully scrutinize.

This role combines research engineering, experimental design, and close technical collaboration. You will move between investigating specific safety questions, navigating complex internal systems, and building reusable tools that make assessments more thorough and efficient. Your work will help turn independent scrutiny into concrete evidence about model capabilities, safeguards, and remaining risks.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Help design assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.

 - Support the technical execution of third-party assessments and embedded audits focused on frontier risks, working with evaluators to translate research questions into experiments, analyses, and evidence requirements.

 - Pair closely with external researchers to provide the data, technical documentation, and context needed to assess models and safeguards. Help them understand relevant system behavior, configurations, and limitations.

 - Design and implement secure access to assessment environments, working with research, engineering, and security teams to make relevant models, tools, and information available.

 - Conduct experiments and run analyses on evaluators’ behalf when direct access is constrained. Develop methods collaboratively, document implementation choices, and make results reproducible and open to challenge.

 - Build tooling that automates auditing, assessment workflows, and internal assurance work, including evidence collection, evaluation execution, and tracking changes across model or safeguard versions.

 - Reproduce external findings, investigate discrepancies with internal results, and work with relevant teams to test proposed mitigations and identify unresolved questions.

 - Document methods, findings, and limitations clearly so that evaluators and internal decision-makers can understand what the evidence establishes and where uncertainty remains.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong software engineering skills and experience building research tools, evaluation infrastructure, or systems for analyzing complex data.

 - Have practical experience working with modern machine learning systems, including designing experiments, running evaluations, and interpreting results.

 - Can navigate unfamiliar codebases and infrastructure, debug across system boundaries, and turn ambiguous research requests into reliable technical implementations.

 - Bring sound judgment to experimental design and measurement, including identifying confounders, limitations, and gaps in evidence.

 - Enjoy working closely with researchers, explaining technical systems, and helping others investigate difficult questions.

 - Value independent scrutiny and can support rigorous assessments that challenge internal assumptions.

 - Have an understanding of, or strong interest in, frontier AI risks, alignment, and the evaluation of safeguards.



Experience with AI safety evaluations, adversarial testing, security research, or technical auditing would be especially relevant.

title: Head of Enterprise Risk Management
description:
About the Team

The OpenAI Risk & Audit team is building an enterprise risk capability for a company operating at the frontier of AI. We help leaders identify, understand, and manage the risks that matter most while enabling responsible innovation and durable growth.

We are developing a modern enterprise risk management (ERM) program and the technology foundation that powers it. Our work connects risk strategy, governance, compliance, and assurance with high-quality data, automated workflows, continuous monitoring, and AI-enabled analysis.

We partner across Finance, Security, Legal, Engineering, Product, People, Operations, and Internal Audit, and provide clear reporting to senior leadership and the Board. We aim to make risk ownership practical, decision-useful, and embedded in how OpenAI builds and scales.

About the Role

As the Head of Enterprise Risk Management, you will help build and lead an integrated ERM program and the ERM platform that supports it. You will establish common risk language, governance, and decision processes while translating them into scalable systems, data products, and workflows.

You will own enterprise risk assessments, maintain a centralized risk register, develop risk appetite and key risk indicators, and help leaders evaluate significant changes such as new products, markets, partnerships, major systems, and strategic investments.

This is a hands-on leadership role at the intersection of risk, operations, and technology. You will work with technical and business teams to connect source systems, improve data quality, automate evidence and control monitoring, and use AI to surface emerging risks and accelerate analysis.

You will also help create a strong risk culture, coordinate assurance across the three lines, and communicate complex issues with clarity and sound judgment. This is an opportunity to build a next-generation capability from the ground up.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and evolve OpenAI’s enterprise risk management framework, including risk taxonomy, governance standards, risk appetite, escalation thresholds, and mitigation expectations.

 - Lead enterprise risk assessments and maintain a centralized, decision-useful risk register that reflects strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, compliance, and emerging risks.

 - Establish key risk indicators, continuous-monitoring capabilities, and executive dashboards that translate complex data into clear signals, trends, and actions.

 - Enable risk-informed change governance for new products, markets, partnerships, acquisitions, major systems, and other high-impact initiatives.

 - Lead effective governance forums working cross-functionally with key partners such as Compliance, Finance, Security and others, and prepare concise reporting for senior leadership and the Board.

 - Define the strategy and roadmap for a modern ERM platform that will connect with systems across the enterprise including identity, finance, HR, ticketing, code, and others through reliable integrations and shared data models.

 - Apply automation, policy-as-code, data analytics, and AI-assisted workflows to evidence collection, control monitoring, issue management, risk analysis, and audit or regulatory responses.

title: SoC Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems.

This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces.

 - Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality.

 - Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components.

 - Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior.

 - Incorporate debug, test, and security requirements into the SoC architecture and implementation, partnering with other silicon designers to make the silicon observable, testable, and secure.

 - Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity.

 - Contribute to power management and security architecture and design.

 - Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up.

 - Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up.

 - Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality.

 - Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up.

 - Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB.

 - Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP.

 - Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links.

 - Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution.

 - Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery.

 - Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system.

 - Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable.

 - Enjoy stretching into multiple domains, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and rolling up your sleeves to build and debug.

 - Enjoy working on a small, dynamic team where priorities evolve and engineers take broad ownership.

 - Are excited about creatively applying automation and AI tools to hardware design and integration work.

About the role

The Senior SRE will be positioned at the intersection of backend engineering, infrastructure operations, and FinOps. The role is explicitly broader than a traditional DevOps engineer and explicitly more hands-on than a pure architect.


What you'll be liable for:

Infrastructure cost efficiency and FinOps. Own the continued reduction of Kubernetes overprovisioning, drive right-sizing programs, and maintain the cost telemetry that backend teams use to make decisions.

GPU throughput optimization. Run a structured experimentation program on on-premise GPU clusters, partnering with AI service owners. Led by the Engineering leadership, with this role providing the experimental bandwidth.

Backend enablement, not ownership absorption. Build the tooling, dashboards, and processes that let backend teams from other groups own their own cost and reliability budgets. The deliverable is leverage, not headcount-shaped work.

Reliability instrumentation. As the infra team owns most of the instrumentation across new and offline flows, this role takes a central seat in making sure that surface area is captured properly for both cost-at-scale and reliability.

Selective security workstreams. Take on a defined slice of the active security work so that senior DevOps engineers are not the single point of execution for security-adjacent platform changes.


We'd love to explore more about you if you have:

This role explicitly requires 4-5 years of hands-on systems experience. We are not looking for someone who will lean entirely on AI tooling to discover what to do; we are looking for someone who already knows what to ask and can use AI tooling as a force multiplier on top of that judgement.

Backend engineering depth: production experience in Python, Go/Rust, comfortable owning services end to end, able to read and reason about backend code across teams.

Kubernetes at scale: scheduler behaviour, resource requests/limits, HPA/VPA, node pool design, cost-aware autoscaling (Cast AI, Karpenter, or equivalent).

Cloud and on-premise infrastructure: GCP fluency, IaC (Terraform), CI/CD, and comfort operating in hybrid setups, including on-prem GPU clusters.

GPU workload understanding: familiarity with throughput profiling, batching, KV-cache behavior, inference server tuning, and GPU utilisation metrics.

Observability and reliability: metrics, traces, logs, SLOs, and the discipline to instrument systems properly rather than reactively.

FinOps mindset: demonstrated history of converting infrastructure choices into measurable cost outcomes.

Security baseline: able to take on platform-security workstreams without requiring constant handoff to the DevOps team.

Can work in the EST time zone (A must)

 - [home-office and connectivity allowance / annual learning budget / parental leave — trim to what's accurate].

You are comfortable going deep — service mesh internals, database internals, distributed-systems failure modes — and equally comfortable defining the reliability and security contracts an enterprise AI platform depends on.

Responsibilities

 - Design, own, and evolve scalable microservices architectures on Kubernetes across GCP, Azure, and AWS, including multi-tenant isolation (namespaces, network policies, per-tenant resource quotas and RBAC).

 - Build core platform and data-plane components in Golang and Python — data ingestion, knowledge-base indexing and vector/graph search, application connectivity, workflow automation, and ML operations — against explicit latency and throughput SLOs.

 - Own service-to-service communication: gRPC/protobuf API contracts, service mesh (Istio/Linkerd), load balancing, retries, timeouts, and circuit breaking.

 - Make and document architectural tradeoffs — partitioning/sharding strategy, consistency models (strong vs. eventual), caching tiers, and build-vs-buy decisions.

 - Define the reliability contract: SLIs/SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, autoscaling (HPA/VPA/KEDA), and graceful degradation.

 - Design and operate the observability stack — Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and real-time alerting — for full visibility into system health.

 - Drive DevOps and platform-engineering practices: IaC (Terraform), Helm, GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux), and CI/CD pipelines.

 - Optimize for performance and cost — profiling, load testing, latency budgets, and cost-per-request.

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience in Platform, Infrastructure, or Backend Engineering.

 - Strong CS fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and networking.

 - Proficiency in Golang and Python.

 - Production experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and microservices architecture.

 - Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (GCP, Azure, or AWS); multi-cloud a strong plus.

 - Strong database expertise: query and read/write-path optimization, partitioning/sharding, replication and consistency models, with practical experience in NoSQL and graph stores. Solid grasp of the CAP theorem and database internals.

 - Solid distributed-systems foundation: idempotency, backpressure, delivery semantics (at-least-once vs. exactly-once), and message queues (Kafka/Pulsar/NATS/PubSub).

 - Track record of building platforms from the ground up that other engineering teams successfully build on.

Bonus

 - Experience operating systems at high scale (high QPS, large data volumes).

 - Depth in auth and security: secrets management (Vault), mTLS, RBAC, OIDC/SAML, network policy.

description:
ABOUT EMA

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.

We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.


BUILD AGENTS THAT LEARN FROM THE WORK THEY DO.

Ema builds AI employees that carry out complex workflows across enterprise applications. Our ML team works on the loop that makes them better: production traces become data, data becomes training and evaluation, and better agents produce better traces. The hard part is deciding which intervention will improve behavior in the next real workflow.



THE PROBLEM SPACE

 - Harnesses and inference-time compute. Design context, tools, skills and orchestration for multi-step agents, including work across documents, slides, images, audio and video. Test where extra reasoning, search or verification earns its latency and cost. Build self-improvement loops with explicit permissions, evaluation gates and rollback.

 - Agent post-training. Curate trajectories for SFT, optimize preferences, or run RL on real agent tasks. Investigate methods such as DPO, GRPO or DAPO where they fit; compare process and outcome supervision, shape rewards, and distill useful frontier behavior into smaller models. Measure whether gains transfer beyond the training environment.

 - Environments and rewards. Turn enterprise workflows into reproducible training and evaluation environments: fixture tenants, simulated users who may get impatient and leave, and rewards grounded in verifiable outcomes. Find the shortcuts an agent can exploit before a training run optimizes for them.

 - Data engines and evaluation. Mine production agent-steps for failures; build curated corpora and useful synthetic augmentation. Calibrate judges against human labels, construct behavior-level benchmarks from real workflows, and quantify data quality, performance uplift and reliability across stochastic runs.

 - Retrieval, memory and context graphs. Connect enterprise information with user- and tenant-level learnings. Separate failures of retrieval from failures to use retrieved context; test what to retain, update and retrieve so that past experience improves the next decision.

 - Quality per dollar. Build and evaluate routing, ensembles, caching and small-model specialization. Measure downstream task success alongside latency and cost; a cheaper model is useful only if the complete agent still succeeds.

You’ll go deep in a subset of these areas. Projects combine applied research with the engineering needed to make the result work in production.



OWN THE EXPERIMENT AND THE SYSTEM

Most projects develop over roughly four to six months, with useful improvements shipping along the way. You’ll define the problem and baseline, build the data or environment needed to test it, run experiments, and own serving and integration. Follow the system through deployment, monitoring and failure analysis until it is ready for a clear engineering handoff.

You’ll work with researchers and engineers across the Bay Area, Vancouver and India. We’re hiring from junior through senior levels, with project scope matched to your experience.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Depth you can defend. Substantial work in at least one of agent/tool-use systems, post-training, reward modeling or RL environments, retrieval and memory, or evaluation design. Be ready to explain the mechanism, the alternatives you rejected and the failure modes you found. One area you can teach us beats five you’ve touched.

 - Evidence of zero-to-one ownership. A system, model or research project you took from an ambiguous problem to a working result. We want to understand your contribution, the tradeoffs you made, and what changed when the work met real users or realistic tasks.

 - Statistical judgment. You can size an experiment, choose meaningful baselines and held-out tests, and account for variation across tasks, seeds and repeated runs. You can distinguish a real improvement from judge bias, data leakage or a benchmark shortcut.

 - Production engineering judgment. You can debug across the model and system boundary, isolate a failure, and turn the result into maintainable production code.

 - Honest measurement. You would rather retire your own approach after a clean negative result than ship an improvement that disappears under a stronger evaluation.

A master’s or PhD in a relevant field, or equivalent work or research experience. Papers, substantial open-source contributions, trained models and well-documented experiments can demonstrate that depth.



EXPERIENCE THAT WOULD BE ESPECIALLY USEFUL

 - Open-model post-training with TRL, veRL, OpenRLHF, or similar or a custom loop, especially debugging reward hacking or unstable optimization.

 - Interactive agent environments/harnesses for software engineering, web or tool use; large-scale trace analysis, data curation or synthetic generation.

 - Designing systems to support complex, long-horizon agent work across a multitude of modalities and platforms

 - Serving with vLLM or SGLang, distillation, quantization, or multi-node GPU training.

 - Practical security work on prompt injection, data governance or permission boundaries for agents that can act and improve themselves.

These are project-specific strengths; post-training experience is optional, and no candidate needs the entire list. Bring a repository, paper, model or technical write-up that lets us examine how you think and what you built.

We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

Who you are

You are an experienced Infrastructure Engineer Engineer who owns backend infrastructure end to end. You design multi-tenant, microservices-based systems that other engineering teams build on, and you make deliberate architectural tradeoffs around consistency, latency, scale, and cost. You are comfortable going deep — service mesh internals, database internals, distributed-systems failure modes — and equally comfortable defining the reliability and security contracts an enterprise AI platform depends on.

Responsibilities

 - Design, own, and evolve scalable microservices architectures on Kubernetes across GCP, Azure, and AWS, including multi-tenant isolation (namespaces, network policies, per-tenant resource quotas and RBAC).

 - Build core platform and data-plane components in Golang and Python — data ingestion, knowledge-base indexing and vector/graph search, application connectivity, workflow automation, and ML operations — against explicit latency and throughput SLOs.

 - Own service-to-service communication: gRPC/protobuf API contracts, service mesh (Istio/Linkerd), load balancing, retries, timeouts, and circuit breaking.

 - Make and document architectural tradeoffs — partitioning/sharding strategy, consistency models (strong vs. eventual), caching tiers, and build-vs-buy decisions.

 - Define the reliability contract: SLIs/SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, autoscaling (HPA/VPA/KEDA), and graceful degradation.

 - Design and operate the observability stack — Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and real-time alerting — for full visibility into system health.

 - Drive DevOps and platform-engineering practices: IaC (Terraform), Helm, GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux), and CI/CD pipelines.

 - Optimize for performance and cost — profiling, load testing, latency budgets, and cost-per-request.

 - Participate in on-call rotations and lead incident response and root-cause analysis.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience in Platform, Infrastructure, or Backend Engineering.

 - Strong CS fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and networking.

 - Proficiency in Golang and Python.

 - Production experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and microservices architecture.

 - Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (GCP, Azure, or AWS); multi-cloud a strong plus.

 - Strong database expertise: query and read/write-path optimization, partitioning/sharding, replication and consistency models, with practical experience in NoSQL and graph stores. Solid grasp of the CAP theorem and database internals.

 - Solid distributed-systems foundation: idempotency, backpressure, delivery semantics (at-least-once vs. exactly-once), and message queues (Kafka/Pulsar/NATS/PubSub).

 - Track record of building platforms from the ground up that other engineering teams successfully build on.

Bonus

 - Experience operating systems at high scale (high QPS, large data volumes).

 - Depth in auth and security: secrets management (Vault), mTLS, RBAC, OIDC/SAML, network policy.

 - Experience with vector databases (pgvector/Pinecone/Milvus) and graph databases (Neo4j/Neptune).

 - Open-source contributions to infrastructure projects (e.g., Kubernetes operators).

The Customer Engagement Manager owns a portfolio of strategic enterprise accounts end-to-end: every engagement, every outcome, every relationship, every expansion opportunity. Think of this as the McKinsey Associate Partner model applied to enterprise AI delivery.

You are the single point of accountability for your accounts. The customer calls you — not your manager — when they have a problem. You staff delivery teams, oversee solution quality, run executive readouts, measure ROI, drive adoption, rebuild trust when things break, and grow the book through proven production value.

This is not a project management role. This is an account ownership role that combines delivery orchestration, outcome ownership, customer leadership, and commercial growth.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

1. Account Ownership

 - Own your accounts end-to-end: every engagement, every outcome, every relationship. Everything good or bad stops with you.

 - Be the single point of contact the customer calls for any problem — delivery, quality, adoption, escalation, or expansion.

 - Maintain a holistic view of each account: engagement status, risk exposure, opportunity pipeline, and the customer’s strategic priorities for the quarter.

 - Run account planning: engagement roadmaps, resource forecasting, risk assessment, and growth strategy.

2. Delivery Orchestration

 - Staff and direct delivery teams (Engineering Leads, Product Managers) across your accounts.

 - Oversee delivery quality across all engagements: review solution architectures, attend go-live rehearsals, ensure evaluation rigor.

 - Manage cross-engagement dependencies within an account (e.g., shared integration infrastructure between parallel deployments).

 - Serve as the delivery escalation point: join war rooms, coordinate fixes across Engineering and Product, and communicate resolution to the customer.

 - You don’t write code — but you review architectures, challenge unrealistic scope, and ensure go-live readiness. Your leverage is orchestration and judgment.

3. Outcome Ownership & Continuous Improvement

 - Own post-go-live outcomes: adoption, ROI, accuracy, and user trust. This role absorbs the Outcomes Manager function for your accounts.

 - Run regular usage readouts: AI deflection rates, false positive/negative trends, HITL escalation patterns, user bypass rates, and trust signals.

 - Separate product gaps from process, training, or expectation gaps. Not everything that looks broken is an engineering problem.

 - Drive continuous improvement cycles: readout → diagnose → prioritize → fix → re-measure.

 - Communicate outcomes in business language: efficiency gains, cost savings, error reduction — not just dashboards, but diagnosis and action plans.

4. Executive Stakeholder Leadership

 - Run QBRs with VP/C-level stakeholders: present outcomes, risks, improvement plans, and the strategic roadmap.

 - Navigate internal customer politics: when the VP of IT and VP of Business disagree on priorities, facilitate alignment around shared success metrics.

 - Communicate bad news credibly: present the data, the diagnosis, and the recovery plan — without losing trust.

 - Handle C-level escalations. When the CTO threatens to terminate or the CFO questions ROI, you are the person in the room.

5. Commercial Growth

 - Grow your book through outcome-driven expansion: deliver the first SOW excellently, measure ROI rigorously, present evidence to the C-suite, then propose the next SOW grounded in proven value.

 - Identify new use cases by deeply understanding customer business processes and pain points — not by pushing a product catalog.

 - Know when to push for expansion vs. when to stabilize. Premature expansion erodes trust. You earn the right to grow by delivering first.

 - Co-sell with Sales: provide the delivery credibility and outcome evidence that makes expansion proposals close.

6. Product & Platform Partnership

 - Act as the voice of your customers to Product and Core Engineering. Translate field patterns into structured, actionable feedback — not one-off requests.

 - Identify cross-customer patterns that signal platform gaps or opportunities.

 - Partner with Product on customer-facing roadmap discussions: what’s coming, what’s not, and how to manage expectations.

7. Team Development

 - Coach Engineering Leads and Implementation Managers on architecture quality, customer communication, delivery discipline, and outcome thinking.

 - Promote shared standards and best practices across engagements.

 - Build reusable account-level assets: engagement playbooks, QBR templates, outcome tracking frameworks, and expansion qualification criteria.




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - 15+ years in enterprise technology delivery, consulting, account management, or customer leadership.

 - 5+ years owning enterprise accounts end-to-end: delivery, outcomes, relationship, and growth — not individual projects within someone else’s account.

 - Track record managing or directing delivery teams (Engineering Leads, TPMs, consultants) assigned to their accounts.

 - Post-go-live outcome ownership: measured ROI, tracked adoption, driven continuous improvement, and rebuilt trust after production issues.

 - Commercial accountability: grown account revenue through outcome-driven expansion, not just retention.

 - Enterprise stakeholder management at VP/C-level across multiple concurrent accounts.

 - Production track record — beyond POCs. Scale and accountability required.

Preferred

 - Experience with AI, automation, or agentic workflow platforms in production.

 - Background at a consulting firm (McKinsey, BCG, Deloitte) or enterprise SaaS PS org (ServiceNow, Salesforce, UiPath) in a delivery-heavy account leadership role.

 - Experience with partner-mediated delivery (delivering through consulting partners to end clients).

 - Familiarity with enterprise integrations (APIs, auth, CRM/HRIS/ITSM platforms) at a judgment level, not implementation level.

 - Experience in a scaling startup ($5M–$50M ARR) where account management practices were being built, not inherited.

description:
ABOUT EMA

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. The residency

You own one hard problem end to end. You write the proposal, build the system, design the evaluation, ship behind a gate, and finish with a write-up of what turned out to be true, including the parts that didn't work. You'll sit in the production codebase with a senior mentor and real production data. Recent residents have shipped self-improving harnesses, inference-cost work, agent memory, and eval infrastructure. Your project gets scoped with you, not handed to you.



The problem space

The loop we care about: production traces become data, data becomes training and evaluation, and better agents produce better traces. Projects live somewhere on that loop.

 - Harness and inference-time work. Context engineering, tool and skill design, orchestration, and deciding where extra inference compute actually pays. Self-improvement loops run behind hard fences.

 - Post-training for agents. SFT on curated trajectories, preference optimization, RL on real agent tasks. Reward design where outcomes are verifiable, process vs. outcome supervision, distilling frontier behavior into cheaper models.

 - Environments and rewards. Turning enterprise workflows into training and eval environments: fixture tenants, simulated users (some of whom get impatient and leave), verifiable rewards, and defenses against reward hacking. Agents will exploit a lazy grader.

 - Data engines. Mining production agent-steps into training and eval corpora: failure mining, labeling with calibrated judges, synthetic augmentation that stays useful.

 - Evaluation. Behavior-level benchmarks from real workflows, LLM judges calibrated against human labels, reliability statistics for stochastic agents.

 - Efficiency. Routing, ensembles, caching, small-model specialization. Quality per dollar is a research metric here.



What we're looking for

 - No specific degree required. Strong undergrads, grad students, and self-taught builders are all welcome; what matters is demonstrated depth in ML or agent systems.

 - Solid ML fundamentals and strong engineering: Python, PyTorch, and the discipline to ship in a large production codebase.

 - Real depth in at least one of: post-training (SFT/DPO/GRPO-family RL), reward modeling or LLM judges, agent and tool-use systems, retrieval and memory, eval design. One area you can teach us beats five you've touched.

 - Statistical literacy. You can size an experiment, and you know 25 samples at one seed is a datapoint, not a result.

 - Honest measurement as a habit. You'd rather kill your own feature with a clean experiment than ship it on a hunch.



Nice to have

 - Hands-on post-training with open models (TRL, veRL, OpenRLHF, or your own loop). Bonus points if you've debugged a reward-hacked run.

 - Built or trained in interactive agent environments (SWE, web, or tool-use gyms).

 - Large-scale trace analysis, data curation, or synthetic data work.

 - Serving and efficiency experience: vLLM/SGLang, distillation, quantization.

 - Multi-node GPU training, or the infra fluency to get there fast.

 - Publications, open-source work, or writing that shows how you think.

 - Security instincts: prompt injection, data governance, why a self-improving agent needs a fence.
   
   

Logistics

 - SF Bay Area, on-site/hybrid, half/full-time for the term. Flexible start.

 - Salary: $4,000 month

description:
ABOUT EMA

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

The role

“The ideal forward deployed builder is a composite. Not a software engineer, not a product manager, not a solutions architect or a salesperson — but able to draw on any of these to solve the customer’s problems, in the customer’s building, on the customer’s timeline, against the customer’s data.”

Ema is building the Universal Agentic Control Plane — the layer where enterprises turn messy, human-run business processes into AI Employees that actually do the work. The platform is powerful. The bottleneck is people who can walk into a customer’s world, see what should be automated, and make it real.

That’s this role.

We’re looking for a Forward Deployed Builder to embed inside our customers and partners, find the highest-value opportunities for agentic automation, solution them, build the demo, win the deal, and then stay to implement it in production. You go in alone, Rambo in the jungle, armed with your wits, your skills, and the most powerful agentic platform on the market. We’ll train you hard before you deploy. After that, the territory is yours.

This is not a support role behind an account team. You are the account team, the solutions architect, and the builder, compressed into one person on the ground. Very few people in the world are doing this today. You’d be among the first.



Where you’ll be

Embedded, in-person, where the work is. You’d work in rotational deployments between your home office and the customers you’re embedded with across EMEA and North America. That could mean six months in London, followed by another six in Bangalore, with six more in New York. If the idea of a rotating tour across EMEA and North America lights you up, keep reading.



What you’ll actually do

 - Hunt for the work worth doing. Sit inside the customer’s operation, learn how they really run, and identify the processes where agentic automation creates outsized value — the ones everyone lives with but no one has fixed.

 - Solution it. Take a tangled, real-world business process and design it into a clean, streamlined agentic flow on Ema. You’ll make the architecture calls: which agents, which integrations, where a human stays in the loop.

 - Build the demo. Get your hands dirty and actually build a working demo — a proof that makes the value undeniable. For partner deployments, that demo becomes their showcase to their customers, so it has to be sharp.

 - Win the technical conversation. Read the room in the moment that matters, own every technical objection, and prove the thing works. You’re the one who makes the solution undeniable — that’s how the deal gets won.

 - Implement it. Turn the won deal into a live, production agentic workflow the customer trusts and adopts. You own the outcome from first conversation to real usage — not a slide, not a pilot that dies, but something running.



Who you are

We don’t care about a rigid list of years and titles. We care that you’re:

 - Technical enough to write some code and use our agentic platform to build a real demo - not just talk about one.

 - Persuasive enough to read an audience and weave a captivating story that ties their pain points to Ema’s value proposition.

 - Product-minded enough to look at a chaotic business process and see the beautiful, streamlined agentic flow hiding inside it.

 - AI-first enough in your day-to-day to drive the impact of ten people — putting agents to work instead of grinding harder.

Most people are strong in one of these. The rare ones are formidable in all four — or hungry enough to become so. That’s who we’re looking for.



The archetypes who would thrive in this role

 - The Management Consultant who wrote code at some point in their life, misses building things, and wants to step into the agentic world for real.

 - The Product Manager who’s tired of owning a sliver and wants to live the entire journey of solving a user’s problem - from the first sales conversation all the way to adoption.

 - The Engineer who’s ready to leave the safety of a Jira backlog and learn to navigate the chaos of a live agentic transformation

 - The Ex-Founder who’s shelved the startup for now and wants to keep their edge sharp - craving operational freedom in an entrepreneurial environment

 - The Wildcard who fits none of the above, but has both the burning passion and the proven skill to deliver. If that’s you, make your case.



Why this role, why now

Agentic AI is the biggest shift in enterprise software in a generation, and the playbook for deploying it is being written right now — by a handful of people. This is your shot to be one of them: to build the muscle, own real outcomes at real companies across two continents, and come out the other side as one of the most capable operators in the agentic world.

We’ll make you deadly. Where you take it is up to you.
