description:
ABOUT EMA

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.

We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.


BUILD AGENTS THAT LEARN FROM THE WORK THEY DO.

Ema builds AI employees that carry out complex workflows across enterprise applications. Our ML team works on the loop that makes them better: production traces become data, data becomes training and evaluation, and better agents produce better traces. The hard part is deciding which intervention will improve behavior in the next real workflow.



THE PROBLEM SPACE

 - Harnesses and inference-time compute. Design context, tools, skills and orchestration for multi-step agents, including work across documents, slides, images, audio and video. Test where extra reasoning, search or verification earns its latency and cost. Build self-improvement loops with explicit permissions, evaluation gates and rollback.

 - Agent post-training. Curate trajectories for SFT, optimize preferences, or run RL on real agent tasks. Investigate methods such as DPO, GRPO or DAPO where they fit; compare process and outcome supervision, shape rewards, and distill useful frontier behavior into smaller models. Measure whether gains transfer beyond the training environment.

 - Environments and rewards. Turn enterprise workflows into reproducible training and evaluation environments: fixture tenants, simulated users who may get impatient and leave, and rewards grounded in verifiable outcomes. Find the shortcuts an agent can exploit before a training run optimizes for them.

 - Data engines and evaluation. Mine production agent-steps for failures; build curated corpora and useful synthetic augmentation. Calibrate judges against human labels, construct behavior-level benchmarks from real workflows, and quantify data quality, performance uplift and reliability across stochastic runs.

 - Retrieval, memory and context graphs. Connect enterprise information with user- and tenant-level learnings. Separate failures of retrieval from failures to use retrieved context; test what to retain, update and retrieve so that past experience improves the next decision.

 - Quality per dollar. Build and evaluate routing, ensembles, caching and small-model specialization. Measure downstream task success alongside latency and cost; a cheaper model is useful only if the complete agent still succeeds.

You’ll go deep in a subset of these areas. Projects combine applied research with the engineering needed to make the result work in production.



OWN THE EXPERIMENT AND THE SYSTEM

Most projects develop over roughly four to six months, with useful improvements shipping along the way. You’ll define the problem and baseline, build the data or environment needed to test it, run experiments, and own serving and integration. Follow the system through deployment, monitoring and failure analysis until it is ready for a clear engineering handoff.

You’ll work with researchers and engineers across the Bay Area, Vancouver and India. We’re hiring from junior through senior levels, with project scope matched to your experience.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Depth you can defend. Substantial work in at least one of agent/tool-use systems, post-training, reward modeling or RL environments, retrieval and memory, or evaluation design. Be ready to explain the mechanism, the alternatives you rejected and the failure modes you found. One area you can teach us beats five you’ve touched.

 - Evidence of zero-to-one ownership. A system, model or research project you took from an ambiguous problem to a working result. We want to understand your contribution, the tradeoffs you made, and what changed when the work met real users or realistic tasks.

 - Statistical judgment. You can size an experiment, choose meaningful baselines and held-out tests, and account for variation across tasks, seeds and repeated runs. You can distinguish a real improvement from judge bias, data leakage or a benchmark shortcut.

 - Production engineering judgment. You can debug across the model and system boundary, isolate a failure, and turn the result into maintainable production code.

 - Honest measurement. You would rather retire your own approach after a clean negative result than ship an improvement that disappears under a stronger evaluation.

A master’s or PhD in a relevant field, or equivalent work or research experience. Papers, substantial open-source contributions, trained models and well-documented experiments can demonstrate that depth.



EXPERIENCE THAT WOULD BE ESPECIALLY USEFUL

 - Open-model post-training with TRL, veRL, OpenRLHF, or similar or a custom loop, especially debugging reward hacking or unstable optimization.

 - Interactive agent environments/harnesses for software engineering, web or tool use; large-scale trace analysis, data curation or synthetic generation.

 - Designing systems to support complex, long-horizon agent work across a multitude of modalities and platforms

 - Serving with vLLM or SGLang, distillation, quantization, or multi-node GPU training.

 - Practical security work on prompt injection, data governance or permission boundaries for agents that can act and improve themselves.

These are project-specific strengths; post-training experience is optional, and no candidate needs the entire list. Bring a repository, paper, model or technical write-up that lets us examine how you think and what you built.

title: Conversation Quality Analyst
description:
ABOUT BOLNA

Bolna is Voice AI infrastructure built for India - and now for the world. We help businesses deploy intelligent voice agents that can call, converse, and convert in any language, at scale. From collections to customer support to sales, our agents handle millions of conversations so humans don’t have to.

We’re a YC F25 company, backed by General Catalyst, with 1,050+ paying customers and growing fast. Our team of ~25 is based in Bengaluru.




THE ROLE

Every voice AI agent Bolna deploys makes real-time judgment calls - when to speak, when to go silent, when a customer is done talking, when to hand off. We’re building automated systems to grade these calls at scale, using LLMs as judges of call quality. But before you trust a model’s judgment, you verify it against a human’s.

That’s this role. You’ll listen to real calls, annotate what actually happened, and check whether our automated systems - LLM-as-judge evals and quantitative signal detection - got it right. It’s precise, high-attention work, and it sits right at the center of how we know our voice agents are actually working.

This is an internship role for someone early in their career who wants hands-on exposure to how a voice AI company builds trust in its own AI.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Annotation

 - Listen to and annotate real customer calls - transcription review, issue tagging, labeling - using tools like Label Studio

 - Follow (and help sharpen) annotation guidelines for a multilingual environment (Hindi, English, Hinglish, )

Verifying LLM-as-Judge Evaluations

 - For calls flagged by our automated eval pipeline, verify whether the model’s call was actually correct - for example, confirming whether a detected barge-in (agent/customer talking over each other) genuinely happened by listening to the audio

 - Mark agreements and disagreements clearly, with reasoning, so we can measure and improve model accuracy over time

 - All tools needed for this will be provided

Verifying Quantitative Measures

 - Check system-flagged quantitative signals against the actual call - e.g., confirming whether an “agent interruption” the system detected really occurred at that timestamp

 - Flag false positives/negatives so we can tighten detection logic

 - Help identify edge cases that current rubrics or detection logic don’t handle well


Inspecting Calls & Surfacing New Issues

 - Regularly inspect calls beyond flagged ones to spot new or emerging issues our rubrics and detection systems don't yet cover

 - Bring these patterns back to the team so rubrics, prompts, and detection logic keep improving




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Must-have

 - Strong attention to detail and the patience to do focused, high-precision work across many calls

 - Multilingual comfort preferred - Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, or Bengali, in addition to English/Hindi

 - Comfortable learning new tools quickly - Label Studio, dashboards, internal QA apps

 - Genuine curiosity about AI and voice AI - you want to understand why a call was flagged, not just complete a checklist

Good to have

 - Any prior exposure to data annotation, labeling, or QA work

 - Familiarity with spreadsheets/basic SQL or comfort reading dashboards (e.g., Metabase)

 - Background in linguistics, call center operations, or content moderation



HOW THIS ROLE GROWS

This is designed as an entry point, not an endpoint. Based on where you show strength, we’ll shape what comes next:

 - Strong rigor and consistency in annotation → QA Lead / Annotation Lead

 - Curiosity about agent logic and how voice AI actually works → Forward Deployed Engineer track

 - Strong pattern recognition and rubric thinking → Data/Eval Engineer, Voice AI Analyst

We’ve seen people join in QA and grow into much broader voice AI builder roles - this is meant to be a real foot in the door, not a dead-end task.



WHY BOLNA

 - Direct exposure to how a fast-growing AI infra company builds trust in its own models

 - Real ownership over a function (call quality) that directly affects what customers see

 - Fastest way to learn the guts of voice AI - ASR, agent logic, eval pipelines - from the ground up

 - Bengaluru office, in-person team collaboration

title: Product Growth Lead
description:
At Bolna, we’re building tools that change how businesses leverage voice AI.

We’re looking for a Product Growth Lead who will work closely with both our Marketing and Product teams to help more users get value from Bolna.

You’ll own lifecycle campaigns and email marketing, build and monitor user funnels, and study how different cohorts adopt the platform. When you find a drop-off, you’ll help address it -whether that means a better email journey, clearer product education, or an experiment with the product managers.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role. You’ll work across user data, lifecycle campaigns, email, and product experiments: finding where different users get stuck, building ways to help them move forward, and measuring what changes.

Our team includes IIT alumni with experience at Bain, Atlassian, Uber, Zomato, and LinkedIn, and is backed by leading investors.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 1. Own the user lifecycle: Build and improve journeys across signup, activation, repeat usage, paid conversion, retention, and reactivation.

 2. Find opportunities in the funnels: Track how users progress through Bolna and identify drop-offs by lifecycle stage, use case, cohort, and product capability.

 3. Drive product adoption: Help users discover and use the features relevant to them, whether they’re building their first agent or expanding an existing deployment.

 4. Run email and lifecycle campaigns: Own audience selection, copy, setup, testing, launch, and measurement for onboarding, product education, feature adoption, and reactivation campaigns.

 5. Turn insights into experiments: Work with engineering, and customer-facing teams to test changes to messaging, onboarding, and the product experience.

 6. Measure what works: Define clear success metrics for each initiative. Look beyond opens and clicks to understand whether users took the next step and continued getting value from Bolna.
    
    


REQUIRED SKILLS

 1. Hands-on growth experience: 3+ years of experience building and running growth or lifecycle programs, with examples of work you personally executed and measured.

 2. Funnel and cohort analysis: Ability to use product data to spot drop-offs, segment users meaningfully, and decide where to focus.

 3. Email marketing: Experience writing, building, testing, and improving automated journeys and targeted campaigns.

 4. Experimentation: Experience forming a hypothesis, launching an experiment, measuring its impact, and iterating based on the results.

 5. Clear writing: Ability to explain a product capability in a way that helps a user understand why and how to use it.

 6. Relevant background: Experience with self-serve SaaS, developer products, product-led growth, or tools like SQL and product analytics is a plus.

 7. Bias toward execution: You’re comfortable getting into the data, writing the email, setting up the campaign, checking the results, and fixing what isn’t working.

 8. Ownership in ambiguity: You can make progress when the problem, audience, or measurement approach hasn’t been fully defined for you.
    
    


WHY JOIN

Backed to build big: Bolna is backed by Y Combinator and leading investors, and we are on a mission to build a generational voice AI company from India.

Rocketship trajectory: We are profitable, growing rapidly, and handling more than 4 million minutes of real conversations every week. You’ll work on growth problems at meaningful scale.

Room to build: You’ll help shape how we understand our users and how we help them succeed, rather than inherit a fixed campaign calendar.

Real ownership: You’ll take ideas from an insight in the data through execution and measurement, with the freedom to improve what you build.

Strong customer feedback loop: You’ll see how developers and businesses use Bolna and turn those insights into better journeys across the product.

Work across the company: You’ll work closely with product, engineering, and customer-facing teams to improve the user experience.

Competitive compensation, meaningful ESOP ownership, health insurance.

 - Work directly with experienced founders and sales leadership who are invested in your success.

 - Benefit from a strong mix of inbound momentum, referrals, investor introductions, and deep industry relationships.

 - Help shape messaging, market strategy, and the sales motion while building your own path for growth.

 - Earn meaningful equity and uncapped commission in a fast-growing company.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the full sales cycle, including discovery, business case development, negotiation, and close.

 - Lead complex deals ranging from $25K to $500K ACV, with room to grow beyond that.

 - Lead with insight: teach buyers something meaningful about their distribution performance before you ever pitch a product

 - Win new logos as the primary motion, and expand relationships as customers see results

 - Represent Outmarket credibly with executive buyers at industry events and through association partnerships.

 - Feed market intelligence back into product, messaging, and leadership decisions.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Proven track record of meeting or exceeding quota, with clear evidence of performance.

 - Experience selling disruptive products or emerging categories where you had to create demand, not just respond to it.

 - Ability to run multiple complex opportunities in parallel with rigor and velocity.

 - Strong communication and storytelling skills, with a focus on business outcomes over features.

 - Comfort operating in a fast-moving, early-stage environment where you build process rather than wait for it.

 - High ownership, strong judgment, and the ability to earn trust quickly with buyers and teammates.


BONUS IF YOU HAVE

WHAT YOU’LL GET

 - Competitive salary and uncapped commission.

 - Meaningful equity in a fast-growing company.

 - Full health, dental, and vision benefits.

 - Remote-first flexibility.

 - Direct access to founders, leadership, and executive buyers from day one.

ABOUT OUTMARKET

Outmarket is an AI-powered platform purpose-built for commercial insurance agencies. We help agencies grow revenue and reduce E&O risk without adding headcount by amplifying what their best people do across every customer engagement and workflow.

We are building for the AI era, where growth can be exponential and operating models must evolve accordingly. Our customers are learning how to compete and win at a new scale using AI, and we are building that same model internally.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring our first Senior Accounting Manager / Controller to lead day-to-day accounting and build the financial infrastructure the company runs on. This is a foundational role for someone who can own the close, build strong systems and controls, and create the reporting foundation that helps take the company from startup to category leader.

You will report to the Head of Finance & Strategy and work closely with finance and leadership. You will own the numbers and the processes behind them, making sure the company can move quickly with confidence in its financial reporting, internal controls, and operating discipline.


WHY THIS ROLE

 - Build the accounting function from the ground up at a company entering its next stage of scale

 - Own the systems, controls, and reporting infrastructure that leadership, the board, and investors will rely on

 - Partner closely with finance and cross-functional leaders on decisions that shape how the company operates

 - Create an AI-native finance stack and help define how automation and intelligent workflows support the accounting function

 - Join a company where the playbook is still being written and your impact will be visible immediately


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the monthly, quarterly, and year-end close, and deliver timely, GAAP-compliant financials that are board- and investor-ready, including ownership of revenue recognition for subscription and usage based 

 - Maintain a clean, well-documented general ledger with account coding that scales as the business grows.

 - Run (and partially automate) AP and AR end to end, including customer invoicing, collections, and expense management.

 - Manage tax compliance and filings, and own relationships with external audit, tax, and legal partners.

 - Build and enforce internal controls, and prepare the company to be audit-ready ahead of future financing rounds and a first external audit.

 - Define and own the AI-native finance tool stack, evaluating and selecting the right systems while identifying where AI can automate and improve workflows.

 - Hire, mentor, and build the accounting team as the function scales.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance. CPA strongly preferred.

 - 5 to 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including experience in a high-growth SaaS company

 - Strong command of U.S. GAAP, financial reporting, and internal controls, including ASC 606 revenue recognition and deferred revenue for subscription & usage businesses.

 - Experience managing month-end close and preparing financial statements, and experience in completing audits.

 - Ability to build sophisticated financial models, automate workflows, and work comfortably with large datasets.

 - A proven track record of building accounting processes in an early-stage environment.


BONUS IF YOU HAVE

 - InsurTech Experience.

 - Big 4 Accounting Experience.

 - Experience with venture-backed startup accounting and external audit or diligence preparation.

 - Experience with accounting process automation, reporting dashboards, and systems integrations.


WHAT YOU’LL GET

 - Direct partnership with finance and leadership at a company defining a new category in commercial insurance.

 - The opportunity to build the accounting foundation and financial operating systems from the ground up.

 - A front-row seat to hyper-growth in the AI era, with real ownership and scope.

 - Competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and clear room to grow.

title: Account Executive
description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client. 
 
  Role type:  Full time 
  Location:  Remote 
  Working days:  Monday–Saturday 
  Working with:  Founders and the customer success team 
 
 Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white-collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them. 
 About the role 
 Every week, founders and talent leads book time with us because hiring in India is broken for them. You take that meeting and you take it all the way to a signed subscription. 
 The pipeline is handed to you. The conversation is not. Thirty minutes with a founder is enough to either earn a customer or lose one, and the difference is almost always how well you understood their hiring problem before you started talking about ours. You'll learn the product deeply enough to search live on a call, quote real candidate supply for their roles, and answer the hard question — "why can't my recruiter just do this?" — without flinching. 
 This is a closing seat, not a coordinating one. You'll be judged on revenue you brought in this month, and you'll know exactly where you stand at all times. Some months that's a great feeling. Some months it isn't. 
 If you need a defined territory, a fixed script, and quarterly reviews to know how you're doing, this will feel uncomfortable. 
 What you'll actually do 
 On any given day you might be: 
 
 Taking booked demos with startup founders, HR leads and talent partners, and diagnosing their hiring problem before pitching anything 
 Showing exactly how our database and outbound campaigns fill the roles sitting open on their careers page 
 Writing follow-ups people actually reply to, and building the case internally for the person championing us 
 Working pricing, paperwork and procurement to done — not to "waiting on them" 
 Reviving deals that went cold, and killing the ones that were never real 
 Bringing objections and lost-deal patterns back to the founders and product team 
 Sitting in on early customer success conversations so what you sell is what gets delivered 
 
 You'll be measured on whether deals closed — well, and on time. Not on activity. 
 What we're looking for 
 
 2+ years selling B2B SaaS or services, with a number you owned and hit 
 You're curious on calls — you ask the second and third question instead of jumping to the demo 
 You can explain a product simply to a founder who has ten minutes and no patience 
 You chase things down. Nothing sits in your pipeline untouched for a week 
 You're straight with people — no overselling, because customer success has to live with what you promise 
 You want to understand recruiting deeply, not just sell software 
 You're comfortable with ambiguity and a Monday–Saturday pace 
 
 What you get 
 
 Warm, qualified demos from day one — you spend your time selling, not prospecting from zero 
 A product built on the largest white-collar talent database in India, with 1000+ companies as proof 
 Direct exposure to the founders and how decisions actually get made 
 A real look at how a profitable, venture-backed startup is built and run 
 Uncapped upside if you can close

 A company books a demo with us because their hiring is stuck. From that first call until they're a paying, active customer, they're yours.

 What you'll actually do

 Running demos of platform.weekday.works with founders and talent leads, and reading what they actually need behind what they say they need

You’d be doing a wide variety of things - talking to the Founding team and CXOs to understand what they are looking for in the crucial person to join their team. title: Data Entry Intern
description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client. 
 
  Role type:  Internship 
  Location:  Remote 
  Duration:  3 months 
  Working days:  Monday–Saturday 
  Stipend:  ₹4,000–5,000/month

 Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them. 
 Read this before you apply 
 This is not a glamorous role. It's careful, high-volume, detail-obsessed work — and the models we're building are only as good as the data you produce. You'll spend your day looking at documents and drawing bounding boxes around the right things: marking exactly where a field, a block of text, a table, or a signature sits on the page, over and over, correctly. It's precise, repetitive work, and it's the foundation the whole annotation project stands on. One sloppy box teaches the model the wrong thing. 
 If you get satisfaction from doing something exactly right, at pace, without cutting corners — you'll do well here. If you need constant variety and get bored by repetition, this isn't for you. 
 What you'll actually do 
 On any given day you might be: 
 
 Looking at documents and drawing accurate bounding boxes around the regions that matter — fields, text blocks, tables, stamps, signatures, whatever the project calls for 
 Labelling and classifying each box correctly according to the annotation guidelines 
 Keeping your boxes tight and consistent — same standard on document one and document one thousand 
 Flagging edge cases, ambiguous documents, and gaps or contradictions in the guidelines instead of guessing 
 Reviewing and correcting your own (and sometimes others') annotations to keep quality high 
 Helping refine the labelling process so annotation gets faster and more consistent over time 
 
 You'll be measured on accuracy, consistency, and throughput — how much high-quality annotated data you produce, not hours logged. 
 What we're looking for 
 
 You're precise and patient — you can draw the same clean box the hundredth time as well as the first 
 You sweat the details; a box that's slightly off or a wrong label bothers you 
 You take ownership. When a batch is yours, it's done right — no follow-ups needed 
 You follow guidelines closely but speak up the moment something doesn't fit them 
 You're comfortable with repetitive, screen-heavy work and a Monday–Saturday pace 
 You care about the quality of your work even when nobody's checking every box 
 
 What you get 
 
 A front-row look at how a venture-backed startup is built and run profitably 
 A real understanding of what goes into the data behind AI models — the part most people never see 
 Real ownership of the ground truth the project depends on 
 A PPO if you perform 
 Hands-on experience with the tools and habits that make you genuinely useful anywhere

title: Founder's Office
description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client.
Role type: Full time
Location: Remote
Working with: CEO and Cofounder
Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them.
 
About the role
You’ll work closely with the founders on some of the most important problems at the company.
There isn’t a fixed lane for this role. What you work on will depend on what the company needs at the time. That could mean figuring out why a product isn’t growing, launching a new product or market, improving an internal process, working with customers, researching a new opportunity, or taking on a project that simply doesn’t have an obvious owner yet.
This is a hands-on role. We’re not looking for someone whose job ends at analysing a problem and making a recommendation. You should be comfortable getting into the details and doing the work yourself.
As the company grows, the problems you work on will change. We expect the role to change with them.
What you’ll work on
Depending on the week, you might:
Take a new idea from a rough hypothesis to something we can actually test
Dig into a part of the business that isn’t working well, understand why, and fix it
Work on growth for an existing product, including talking to customers, improving positioning, running experiments, or helping close important deals
Research a new market, product, partnership, or business opportunity and decide whether it is worth pursuing
Build a process or internal tool where none exists today
Work with product and engineering to turn customer or business problems into product changes
Take ownership of projects that cut across teams and would otherwise fall between the cracks
Help the founders make decisions by getting to the underlying facts quickly
Some projects will last a few days. Others may become something you own for months.
What we’re looking for
You’re good at figuring things out. You can take a vaguely defined problem, ask the right questions, and get to a useful answer without needing a detailed brief.
You’re comfortable doing the work yourself. If something requires talking to customers, going through data, writing copy, building a spreadsheet, or putting together a quick script, you’ll do it.
You have good business judgement. You can distinguish between something that is interesting and something that actually matters.
You’re comfortable with numbers and technology. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be able to work with data and use technology to make yourself more effective.
You communicate clearly. You can write well, explain what you’ve learned, and say when something isn’t working.
You take ownership. Once you take something on, the founders shouldn’t have to keep checking whether it is moving.
You care about details. A lot of this job involves noticing things other people miss and following through on them.
You’re comfortable with ambiguity. Priorities will change and you won’t always have a playbook to follow.
We care less about whether you’ve had a “Founder’s Office” title before. You could come from startups, consulting, product, growth, operations, investing, or something else entirely. What matters is whether you can learn quickly and get useful things done.
What you get
You’ll work directly with the founders and get exposure to most parts of the company.
You’ll see how decisions get made, work on problems before they have dedicated teams around them, and have a lot of room to take ownership. If something you start becomes important enough, there’s a good chance you’ll continue to own it.
This role is a good fit for someone who eventually wants to build a company, run a business or product line, or become a generalist operator at an early-stage company.

About the role
This is a growth role, not a strategy role. You will sit next to the CEO and own one number: revenue growth for one of our core product lines. Everything you do — every piece of content, every cold email, every demo call — either moves that number or it doesn't.
You won't be handed a playbook, a team, or a warmed-up pipeline. You'll build the GTM engine yourself: figure out which channels work, build them, and scale the ones that do. Some weeks that means writing content and tuning SEO/AEO so buyers find us. Other weeks it means running demo calls back-to-back and following up aggressively until deals close. If you think of yourself as either "a marketer" or "a salesperson" but not both, this isn't for you.
What you'll actually do
On any given day you might be:
Running the full inside-sales motion — taking demo calls, handling objections, following up relentlessly, and closing
Building content that actually converts: landing pages, comparison pages, blog posts, and material designed to rank on search and get picked up by AI answer engines (AEO)
Setting up and running outbound systems — cold email, cold calls, LinkedIn, or whatever channel gets us in front of the right buyers
Writing scripts and light automations to scale yourself — scraping lead lists, wiring up email sequences, building dashboards so you know what's working
Testing a new growth channel, killing it fast if it doesn't work, and doubling down if it does
Reporting your numbers honestly to the founders, including the ugly ones
You'll be measured on revenue — pipeline created and deals closed. Not on activity, not on slides.
What we're looking for
You can sell. You're sharp on calls, you can run a demo that lands, and you follow up like the deal depends on it — because it does.

 Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white-collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them. 
 About the role 
 We help hundreds of companies hire. This role is about hiring for ourselves — and looking after the people once they're here. 
 Your week will be roughly half talent acquisition and half people ops. One morning you're sourcing candidates for an ops role using the same database and outbound tools our customers pay for. That afternoon you're onboarding a new joiner, chasing payroll inputs, or sorting out a leave policy question nobody has asked before. 
 This is not a "post the JD and wait" recruiting job, and it's not an "HR admin in a back office" job. You will be close to the founders, you will see every hire we make, and you will be the person the team comes to when something people-related needs fixing. 
   
 What you'll actually do

 Sourcing and running outbound to candidates for Weekday's own roles — ops, sales, customer success, engineering, interns — using the Weekday platform

 You move fast and figure things out without a playbook — and when there's no process, you write one.

title: People Lead (Talent Acquisition & HR)
description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client. 
 
  Role type:  Full time 
  Location:  Remote and/or Bangalore 
  Working days:  Monday–Saturday 
  Working with:  Founders (mostly CEO & COO) 
 
 Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white-collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them. 
 About the role 
 We're a recruiting company. That means the bar for how we hire our own team is higher, not lower. If our own hiring is slow or sloppy, we have no business selling hiring to anyone else. 
 This role owns both halves of people at Weekday: bringing the right people in, and building the place they want to stay. Roughly half your time goes into talent acquisition — planning hiring with the founders, running pipelines, closing senior candidates. The other half goes into HR — policies, performance, compensation, engagement, compliance — for a team of around 50–70 people that keeps growing. 
 There is no HR department waiting for you. There is some process, some of it good, much of it built on the fly. You'll decide what to keep, what to fix, and what to build from scratch. You'll do the work yourself before you hire anyone to do it for you. 
 What you'll actually do 
 On any given day you might be: 
 
 Working with the founders on the hiring plan and owning it: which roles, in what order, at what bar 
 Running senior and hard-to-fill hires yourself — sourcing on the Weekday platform, pitching, closing, negotiating 
 Setting up the hiring machine: scorecards, interview loops, work trials, and a candidate experience we'd be proud to show customers 
 Designing and running performance reviews, goal-setting, and feedback cycles that people actually take seriously 
 Building the basics properly: policies, compensation bands, leave, payroll, and labour-law compliance 
 Owning onboarding, engagement, and retention — and reading attrition data honestly, including the ugly numbers 
 Being the person the team trusts with hard conversations — conflicts, underperformance, exits 
 
 You'll be measured on whether things got done — well, and on time. Not on slides. 
 Who you are 
 
 2–5 years across talent acquisition and HR. You've been the first or second people hire somewhere, or you've built people ops at a startup that was scaling fast. 
 You've recruited hands-on and closed senior hires yourself — not just managed agencies. 
 You have strong judgment on people. You can tell a good hire from a good interviewer. 
 You're a builder, not a policy-keeper. You write the process when there isn't one, and you cut it when it stops helping. 
 You communicate directly — no padding, no spin — and you can say no to a founder when it's the right call. 
 You know Indian labour law and payroll basics well enough to keep us compliant without a consultant on speed dial. 
 You're comfortable with ambiguity and a Monday–Saturday pace. 
 
 Nice to have 
 
 Experience at a recruiting, HR-tech, or staffing company 
 Comfort with tools like Airtable, Slack, Notion, or an HRMS - and a habit of automating repetitive work 
 
 What you get 
 
 Full ownership of people function at a profitable, venture-backed startup - the culture you build is the one that sticks 
 Direct partnership with the founders on every hiring and people decision 
 India's largest white-collar talent database and our outbound tools, for your own hiring 
 A front-row seat to how a company scales, and the chance to build the team that does it

🚀 Why Join Weekday?
At Weekday, we are building the future of startup hiring. High-growth tech companies and fast-paced startups rely on us to find exceptional talent, fast.
As a Talent Operations Associate Consultant, you will be on the front lines evaluating top-tier talent, conducting research on cutting-edge roles, and running the evaluation engine that connects great candidates with world-class tech companies.
If you are early in your career and looking for a fast-tracked growth opportunity into talent acquisition, startup operations, or people management, this is your launching pad.
 
💡 What You’ll Do (Your Impact)
Conduct High-Impact Candidate Screenings: Lead intro & evaluation calls with candidates to assess their technical/non-technical fit against client company requirements.
Deep-Dive Role Research: Research client roles upfront so you can lead engage-and-answer discussions and guide candidates authoritatively through the process.
Capture Rigorous Data & Evaluation: Collect comprehensive candidate insights covering structured rubric points to ensure candidates meet client interview standards.
Manage Candidate Experience & Feedback: Own candidate communication from end to end, managing feedback loops, status updates, and handoffs to Account Managers.
Master Talent Operations Tools: Leverage modern recruiting and operational software (Airtable, Slack, CRM tools) to deliver accurate reporting and maintain high quality standards.
Fast-Track POD Leadership: Step up into a POD Lead role—guiding a sub-team of 2–3 associates, driving daily operational targets, coaching team members, and helping scale your POD to maintain high screening standards. 
🎯 Who You Are
We are looking for self-starters who are eager to learn and execute with excellence. You will thrive in this role if you are:
An Early Career Professional or Fresh Graduate: You have 0–1 years of experience (Graduates in BBA, Psychology, Engineering, or related fields are highly encouraged to apply!).
An Exceptional Communicator: You possess fluent written and spoken English skills with the confidence to lead candidate calls professionally.
A Fast Learner & Research-Minded: You can quickly grasp job descriptions across technical and non-technical domains and synthesize information quickly.
Coachable & Action-Oriented: You absorb feedback rapidly, adapt to fast-changing environments, and enjoy hitting daily operational goals.
Aspiring Leader: You are eager to move beyond individual execution and take on pod leadership, team coaching, and operational performance tracking early in your career. 
Bonus points if you have experience with Airtable/Slack or a strong interest in startup hiring!
 
📈 What Your First 90 Days Look Like
First 15 Days (Onboard & Learn): Shadow live screening calls, master internal documentation tools, begin independently conducting 15–20 screening calls/day and progressively ramp up screening volume (target: 25–40 calls/day). 
Days 30–60 (Own & Lead): Run high-quality candidate screens independently while taking on POD Lead responsibilities—coaching a sub-team of 2–3 members, tracking daily metrics, and driving corrective actions to ensure target completion.
Towards 6 Months (Scale & Convert): Help build and mentor your POD team (scaling toward 5 structured PODs across the team) while positioning yourself for contract extension or full-time conversion.
🎁 What’s In It For You?
Direct Path to Full-Time: Outstanding performance directly opens doors for extension of contract or conversion to full-time.
Steep Learning Curve: Learn startup hiring, candidate evaluation, and operational analytics directly from experienced leaders.
Culture of Growth: Work in a high-energy environment where taking ownership is recognized and rewarded.
📋 The Hiring Process

Recruiter Screen (20 mins): Intro call to discuss your goals, background, and alignment.
Hiring Manager Screen & Live Mock Call (30–45 mins): Practical assessment to showcase your research mindset, communication clarity, and coachability with Meghana, who this role will be reporting to.

We are seeking a Head of Global Partnerships to architect, lead, and scale Jeeves' partner ecosystem across our most strategic regions: North America, Latin America (focused on BR, MX, & CO), and EMEA. Reporting directly to the CRO, this leader will own the full partnerships vision — from setting the global framework to closing the deals that matter most.
This is a role for a builder who thinks in ecosystems, not channels. The best partnerships leaders we've seen don't specialize in one type of partner — they've built playbooks for many: stablecoin and crypto networks, banks and financial institutions, brokers, technology platforms, advisory firms, accounting networks, marketplaces, VC/PE ecosystems, embedded finance players, and models we haven't thought of yet. title: Senior Business Analyst, Credit & Analytics
description:
Jeeves is the stablecoin-native banking platform for global enterprises. Thousands of companies across 35 countries run their corporate cards, payments, treasury and spend on one platform, with more than $5B in annualized volume, payouts to 190 countries, and one of the fastest-growing stablecoin payment networks in the world. BMW, H&M, Lululemon, Burger King, Kavak and XP are among them, and more than 80% of customers use multiple Jeeves products.
We chose hard problems on purpose.
We hire for one thing: relentlessness. A strong motor that keeps going when the problem has no playbook. You'll know in your first week if Jeeves is right for you. For the right people, it's the steepest learning curve of your career.
Jeeves has raised more than $400 million in equity funding from Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, CRV, Coinbase Ventures, GIC, AllianceBernstein, CoinFund and others.
If you want to rebuild how money moves across borders, come build it with us.


Jeeves extends credit to thousands of businesses across Latin America and beyond, and the quality of those decisions depends on the quality of our data. Our Credit & Analytics team has a clear roadmap: reliable portfolio monitoring, better risk models, and more automated credit decisioning. All of it depends on first getting our data foundation right — connecting and maintaining external data sources and cleaning up customer data consents — and today that work competes with day-to-day execution for the same few people.
We're looking for a hands-on Senior Business Analyst to own that foundation and build on it. In your first months you'll lead the work to connect and validate external data (bureau, banking, open finance and tax data), clean up consent records so we can use that data reliably, and turn manual processes into repeatable ones. From there you'll use that data to shape credit policy: underwriting criteria, credit limit strategies, portfolio monitoring and early-warning signals that help us catch losses before they happen.
This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who likes to get into the data themselves. You'll partner closely with data science, engineering, product, collections and sales, and your work will directly shape how Jeeves makes credit decisions as we scale. It is not a people-management role today.
Location: This is a full-time remote position. #LI-REMOTE

description:

We chose hard problems on purpose.
We hire for one thing: relentlessness. A strong motor that keeps going when the problem has no playbook. You'll know in your first week if Jeeves is right for you. For the right people, it's the steepest learning curve of your career.
Jeeves has raised more than $400 million in equity funding from Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, CRV, Coinbase Ventures, GIC, AllianceBernstein, CoinFund and others.
If you want to rebuild how money moves across borders, come build it with us.


Brazil is one of Jeeves's fastest-growing markets, and the number of companies applying for our corporate cards there keeps climbing. Every one of those applications needs a thoughtful credit decision, and every approved account needs to be watched over time. Today that work sits largely with one senior underwriter. We're adding an Underwriter to the team so we can keep decisions fast and sound as volume grows, and so the Brazil book is never dependent on a single person.
Alongside traditional credit analysis, our underwriters work closely with AI tools that help organize borrower data, draft parts of the analysis and surface questions worth asking. The judgment and the final call stay with you. We're continually moving more of our workflow onto AI, and you'll be part of shaping how that happens. If you're excited by the idea of building the next version of underwriting while practicing the fundamentals, this role is for you.
You'll work side by side with our senior underwriter in Brazil, analyzing new applications from startups and SMBs, preparing credit recommendations, and helping monitor the existing portfolio for early signs of stress. You'll learn how our scoring models work and when judgment needs to go beyond the model, and you'll build the kind of context on the book that lets you cover confidently when your teammate is out. You'll also work closely with our Sales and Account Management teams in Brazil, who rely on clear, timely answers.
This is a hands-on analyst role with real ownership of a growing share of the queue. You won't hold final approval authority on day one — you'll earn more of it as you build judgment and a track record — and there's a clear path to growing into a senior underwriting role as Brazil scales.
Location: This role is based out of São Paulo and is a full-time hybrid position where it is required to come into our office in São Paulo. #LI-HYBRID

title: Analyst, Banking Alliances
description:
Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution.

Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.

From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech

Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.

Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.

Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.

We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.

But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors,  you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.

 

 About the Role 

We are looking for a driven and knowledgeable Sales Manager to lead Payment Gateway (PG) business growth across strategic high potential locations. The ideal candidate will have a strong grasp of the payments ecosystem, hands-on experience working with banks and financial institutions, and the ability to build and leverage government relationships to drive adoption and revenue. 

Key Responsibilities 

Payment Gateway Sales & Business Development 

• Own end-to-end sales of PG solutions to merchants, enterprises, and institutions in the assigned strategic location 

• Identify, prospect, and close high-value merchants across sectors such as retail, education, healthcare, and government 

• Drive acquisition of new accounts while growing revenue from existing merchant partnerships 

• Pitch and position PG products including payment links, UPI, cards, EMI, and BNPL solutions based on merchant needs 

Bank & Financial Institution Management 

• Build and maintain strong relationships with regional and cooperative banks, NBFCs, and nodal banking partners 

• Lead commercial negotiations including MDR, settlement cycles, credit limits, and partnership terms 

• Coordinate with bank partners for faster onboarding, issue resolution, and co-selling opportunities 

• Stay updated on RBI guidelines, banking circulars, and compliance requirements affecting PG operations 

Government & Institutional Relationships 

• Develop and manage relationships with state and local government bodies, PSUs, and municipalities for PG adoption in public services 

• Identify and pursue opportunities in government collections — utility payments, tax portals, welfare disbursements, and e-governance projects 

• Represent the company in government tenders, RFPs, and empanelment processes 

• Liaise with government officials and decision-makers to position the company as a preferred payments partner 

Commercial Negotiation & Deal Structuring 

• Lead pricing discussions and commercial structuring for large and strategic deals 

• Collaborate with internal product, risk, and finance teams to create customized proposals 

• Ensure deal profitability while maintaining competitive positioning in the market 

Market Intelligence & Reporting 

• Track competitor activity, pricing trends, and emerging merchant needs across assigned strategic locations 

• Provide regular pipeline reports, forecasts, and market insights to regional leadership 

• Represent ground-level feedback to product teams for localization and feature improvements 

What We're Looking For 

Must-Have Skills & Experience 

• 4–8 years of experience in Payment Gateway, Fintech, or Banking sales 

• Deep understanding of PG infrastructure — acquiring banks, payment networks, settlement flows, risk & compliance 

• Proven track record of commercial negotiation with banks or financial institutions 

• Experience managing or engaging with government bodies or PSUs for payments/fintech solutions 

• Strong hunter mentality with a consultative sales approach 

• Excellent communication, relationship management, and stakeholder influence skills 

Good to Have 

• Prior experience working in or extensively covering the assigned strategic location 

• Existing network of merchants, bank officials, or government contacts in Chandigarh, Lucknow, Chennai, Hyderabad, or Kolkata 

• Familiarity with RBI payment regulations, PCI-DSS, and digital payment policies 

• Understanding of GST, e-invoicing, or government payment use cases 

Razorpay believes in and follows an equal employment opportunity policy that doesn't discriminate on gender, religion, sexual orientation, colour, nationality, age, etc. We welcome interests and applications from all groups and communities across the globe.
 
Follow us on LinkedIn & Twitter

Forward-Deployed Engineer, Agent Studio

About Agent Studio

Agent Studio helps Razorpay merchants run AI agents across payments, checkout, disputes, subscriptions, reconciliation, risk, and customer workflows. We take the messy, undocumented work merchants do every day and turn it into reliable production agents.

The role

We're hiring a Forward-Deployed Engineer who is equal parts engineer, solution consultant, and merchant partner — the single technical owner of the merchant relationship. You'll sit directly with strategic merchants, run the discovery, find the real constraint behind the ask, design the solution, build the first working version, prove whether it moved the metric, and expand from there.

This is a deeply customer-facing role. You'll own the conversation — not hand it off. You'll walk into a room where the business owner, the ops lead, and the dashboard all tell different stories, and you'll be the one who reconciles them into a spec everyone agrees to ship. Then you'll go build it. You earn the customer's trust because you can do both — reshape the ask and write the code.

If you like being close to the problem, comfortable in front of customers, and can ship, this is for you.

What you'll own

Customer discovery & the relationship

  • Own merchant conversations end-to-end — discovery calls, workshops, solution reviews, and rollout check-ins. You're the merchant's trusted technical advisor.
  • Sit inside merchant workflows long enough to understand the real process, not the documented one. Ask who actually does the work and what happens when it fails.
  • Reconcile conflicting signals across business owners, operators, dashboards, CRM, and ticket queues into a clear problem statement.

Solution design & consulting

  • Name the business constraint behind the ask: checkout recovery, dispute win rate, RTO loss, SIP recovery, settlement delay, refund spikes, support load, or cashflow leakage.
  • Convert fuzzy merchant problems into crisp agent specs: success metric, data sources, tool calls, guardrails, human-in-the-loop points, and rollout plan.
  • Decide what the agent does on its own, what it recommends, and where a human must approve.
  • Write the spec clearly enough that product, engineering, legal, and the merchant all agree on what ships.

Hands-on build & integration

  • Build prototypes, connectors, MCP tool specs, eval fixtures, dashboards, and the glue code that gets an agent into production.
  • Debug integration failures across Razorpay systems, merchant systems, external tools, and model behavior.
  • Deploy across the constraints that real merchants have — auth, networking, data access, latency, cost per run, observability, and compliance — and keep them in the design from day one.

Proof, expansion & productization

  • Set quality gates and outcome metrics before rollout. Track production outcomes, not demo applause.
  • Measure whether the agent moved the target metric. If it didn't, diagnose and fix — or kill it with evidence.
  • Drive expansion through building: spot the next high-value use case, prototype it, and deepen the merchant's agent footprint over time.
  • Turn repeated field patterns into reusable Agent Studio capabilities — connectors, templates, eval packs, docs, platform requirements. You are the field voice that shapes what the platform builds next.

You may be a fit if you

  • Have 3+ years shipping production software, and are strong in Python or TypeScript.
  • Have worked directly with customers, enterprise stakeholders, or operators — and are comfortable owning the room and the technical relationship.
  • Have hands-on experience with APIs, webhooks, auth, data pipelines, and production debugging.
  • Have practical LLM/agent experience: prompts, tool calling, RAG, evals, or workflow automation.
  • Prefer ambiguous, high-context problems over clean tickets.
  • Take ambiguous problems, define the structure, and drive them to resolution 
  • Write clearly — specs, implementation plans, and crisp follow-ups.

Strong pluses

  • Prior shape: solutions engineer, solution consultant, sales engineer, founding engineer, product engineer, applied AI engineer, or an operator who wrote code.
  • Payments, fintech, ecommerce, subscriptions, risk, reconciliation, settlement, or finance-ops experience.
  • Worked with MCP servers, agent skills, multi-agent workflows, eval harnesses, or LLM observability.
  • Enterprise integration experience: private connectors, VPC/on-prem constraints, SOC2/ISO reviews.

What this role is not

  • Not a pre-sales demo role where success is a slick walkthrough.
  • Not a pure implementation role where success is shipping whatever the merchant asked for.
  • Not a support role where success is closing tickets.
  • Not a research role where success is a clever agent that never reaches production.

Job Title - Analyst - Risk Management 

The Role: 

The role will involve establishing and nurturing relationships with channel partners to promote and sell our products or services. You will play a critical role in expanding our business through strategic partnerships and ensuring the successful onboarding of new partners. 

Job Summary 

This role requires strong knowledge and experience in Sanctions, AML (Anti-Money Laundering), and Financial Crimes. The position will focus on Customer Due Diligence (CDD), website assessment, risk assessment associated with merchant onboarding, and Transaction Monitoring, covering all aspects of business model validation and compliance. 

Roles and Responsibilities 

  • Conduct onboarding and ongoing customer due diligence. 
  • Conduct and perform quality control relative to a variety of investigation types, including suspicious activity, sanctions, and enhanced due diligence (EDD). 
  • Manage daily escalation queues, handling complex or exception cases from business and operations teams. 
  • Participate in process improvement, identifying and implementing best practices in effective and innovative ways. 
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) with comprehensive knowledge about AML policies, fraud control, risk categorization policies, monitoring, evaluation, review, and associated reporting. 
  • Demonstrate excellent knowledge of reporting procedures and record-keeping guidelines. 
  • Maintain the ability to communicate clearly and precisely to the point with stakeholders.
  • ● Should be familiar with essential screening tools, including Dow Jones and LexisNexis. 

Qualifications Required

○ Knowledge about a customer support application or CRM, such as Freshdesk.

○ Familiarity with Stages/levels of chargebacks, penalty involved at the arbitration stage, technical chargebacks, Visa/Mastercard guidelines (in brief), and reason codes in relation to fraud chargebacks. 

Core Skills: 

○ Communication Skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication.

○ Listening Skills: Ability to understand, anticipate, and resolve queries arising from various stakeholders.

○ Attention to Detail and Accuracy: Excellent organizational and multitasking skills, with the ability to identify anomalies or suspicious behaviors.

○ Bachelor's Degree.

Art direction and brand
Set creative direction for product marketing content, GTMs, feature launches, and advertising campaigns across countries — shoots, storyboards,

The Roles and Responsibilities:

AEO Strategy & Execution

  • Develop and execute Razorpay’s AEO strategy aligned with AOP, quarterly goals, and monthly objectives , with clear KPIs around AI answer visibility, brand mention share, and citation rates.
  • Build and maintain an AEO performance dashboard tracking Razorpay’s visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and other answer engines.
  • Monitor AEO positioning across key payment platforms, tracking how leading domestic and global players are referenced in AI-generated responses.
  • Define and track Razorpay’s “Agentic Readiness Score” , measuring how well Razorpay’s website, docs, and content are structured for AI agent consumption.

Content Optimization for AI

  • Audit and optimize Razorpay’s existing content (website, blog, docs, learn pages) for AI retrieval , ensuring structured data, clear entity relationships, and answer-ready formatting.
  • Develop content strategies specifically designed to win AI citations , including comparison pages, FAQ schemas, definitive guides, and structured product narratives.
  • Collaborate with the content team to create authoritative, entity-rich content that positions Razorpay as the primary source for payments and fintech topics in LLM training and retrieval.
  • Implement and maintain schema markup, structured data, and semantic HTML optimizations that improve AI comprehension of Razorpay’s content.
  • Develop guidelines for RAG-optimized content architecture — defining how pages should be structured (header hierarchies, summary blocks, definition-first writing, explicit claim statements) so that retrieval systems consistently surface the most relevant Razorpay passage for a given query, rather than a competitor's.

Technical AEO & Website Readiness

  • Work with engineering to ensure Razorpay’s website architecture supports AI crawlers, agents, and retrieval systems , including proper robots.txt directives, API endpoints for agentic access, and clean information architecture.
  • Conduct regular technical audits focused on AI readiness , crawlability by AI bots, structured data integrity, content freshness signals, and page experience metrics.
  • Optimize site speed, mobile experience, and Core Web Vitals as baseline requirements for both traditional SEO and AI answer eligibility.
  • Monitor and resolve technical issues impacting AI visibility , including indexing gaps, stale content, and broken structured data.
  • Own Razorpay’s agentic AI readiness , ensure all key surfaces (website, developer docs, pricing pages, product pages, integration guides) are structured for autonomous AI agents to navigate, extract information, and take action without human intervention.
  • Drive agentic AI onboarding readiness , work with Product and Engineering to ensure Razorpay’s signup, KYC, and merchant onboarding flows are parseable and completable by AI agents acting on behalf of prospective merchants, including structured form data, clear step sequencing, and machine-readable eligibility criteria.
  • Define and maintain agentic interface standards , including machine-readable sitemaps, API-accessible content layers, agent-friendly navigation patterns, and llms.txt or equivalent protocols that enable AI agents to understand and interact with Razorpay’s digital ecosystem.

AEO Tool Stack & Measurement

  • Evaluate, implement, and manage the AEO tool stack (e.g., Otterly.ai, Slate, Profound, Peec AI, and emerging platforms) for tracking AI answer visibility and brand mentions.
  • Build measurement frameworks that quantify AEO impact on pipeline, traffic, and brand perception , establishing AEO as a reportable marketing channel.
  • Design and run experiments to test content formats, structural changes, and optimization tactics that improve AI answer outcomes.
  • Stay ahead of LLM ranking factors, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns, and AI search algorithm updates , translating them into actionable playbooks.
  • Own Razorpay's GA4 implementation as it relates to AEO and organic performance, including custom event tracking, conversion path analysis, channel grouping configurations, and funnel attribution — to accurately measure how AI-referred and organic traffic behaves across Razorpay's product pages, docs, and sign-up flows.
  • Build GA4-based reporting layers that connect AEO visibility metrics (AI citations, answer impressions) to downstream business outcomes (sessions, sign-up initiations, product page depth), enabling leadership to see AEO's contribution to pipeline. not just traffic.

AI-Powered Automation & Workflows

  • Design and build automated SEO/AEO dashboards that pull data from multiple sources (Google Search Console, Ahrefs, AEO tracking tools, GA4) into unified, real-time views , eliminating manual reporting overhead.
  • Build AI-driven content generation workflows , automated brief creation, first-draft generation, meta tag optimization, and bulk content updates powered by LLMs with human-in-the-loop quality gates.
  • Create automated recommendation engines that surface SEO/AEO optimization opportunities , flagging underperforming pages, suggesting content gaps, recommending internal linking improvements, and prioritizing fixes by impact.
  • Build end-to-end workflow automations using AI tools, APIs, and platforms (e.g., Zapier, Make.com, n8n, Claude API, custom scripts) to streamline repetitive SEO/AEO operations across content, technical, and reporting functions.
  • Automate content refresh and decay detection workflows , identifying stale content, triggering update cycles, and auto-generating refresh briefs based on search trend shifts and AI answer changes.
  • Create self-serve automation templates that enable the broader marketing team to run SEO/AEO tasks (keyword research, content audits, performance pulls) without manual intervention.
  • Continuously identify automation opportunities across the SEO/AEO function , with a target of reducing manual effort by 50%+ within the first year through intelligent automation.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with SEO, Performance Marketing, Brand, and Product Marketing teams to ensure AEO strategy is integrated with broader marketing efforts.
  • Work with Product and Engineering teams on developer documentation optimization , a critical surface for AI-driven recommendations in the payments space.
  • Manage relationships with external SEO/AEO vendors, consultants, and platform providers.
  • Present AEO performance reports, insights, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership including CPO and CMO.

Mandatory Skills:

  • 5 to 7 years of experience in SEO, with at least 1-2 years of direct exposure to AEO, AI search optimization, or LLM-related content strategy.
  • Deep understanding of how LLMs (GPT, Gemini, Claude, Llama) retrieve, rank, and cite web content , including RAG systems, knowledge graphs, and entity recognition.
  • Hands-on experience building automation workflows and AI agents using AI tools, APIs, and platforms (Zapier, Make.com, n8n, Python scripting, or similar) , not just using tools, but architecting end-to-end automated pipelines.
  • Deep hands-on experience with GA4, custom dimensions, event schema design, funnel exploration, attribution modelling, and Looker Studio or BigQuery integration for advanced reporting. Ability to go beyond out-of-the-box reports and build measurement frameworks that accurately reflect non-linear, multi-touch journeys typical of B2B fintech discovery.
  • Proven ability to build dashboards and automated reporting systems , pulling data from multiple sources into unified views using tools like Looker Studio, Tableau, Google Sheets with APIs, or custom solutions.
  • Strong technical SEO foundation , site architecture, JavaScript for SEO/AEO, crawl optimization, and mobile-first indexing.
  • Experience with AI-powered content generation and SEO workflows , using AI Agents for automated brief creation, content drafting, meta tag generation, or bulk optimization at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with SEO tools (Ahrefs, SEMrush, Screaming Frog, Google Search Console) and emerging AEO tools (Otterly.ai, Profound, or similar).
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to present to senior leadership and influence cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, or payments is strongly preferred.

Good to Have

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, given the role's hands-on requirements around automation pipelines, API integrations, and RAG-layer content architecture, a foundational technical education accelerates ramp-up significantly.
  • Experience with content strategy for developer audiences (API docs, technical guides, integration tutorials).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML fundamentals , understanding of embeddings, vector search, and how AI models process content.
  • Proficiency in Python or JavaScript for custom automation scripts, API integrations, and data pipelines.
  • Experience with Claude API, OpenAI API, or similar LLM APIs for building production-grade content and recommendation workflows.
  • Experience managing external agencies or vendors in an SEO/content capacity.
  • People management experience , ability to lead and mentor a small team as the AEO function scales.
  • Track record of experimentation , designing A/B tests, content experiments, and iterating based on data.
  • Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol), AI agents, or agentic workflow frameworks.

Roles and  Responsibilities

Role Summary

The Technical Account Manager owns the technical relationship with Razorpay's most strategic global customers. You are accountable for both reactive excellence—owning high-priority incidents and escalations through to resolution—and proactive account health—identifying risks before they become incidents, driving remediation plans, and serving as the customer's trusted technical advisor.

This is not an escalation coordinator or ticket manager role. This is the technical owner of enterprise customer outcomes.

What You Will Own

Reactive Ownership

  • Own incidents end-to-end — coordinate Engineering, SRA, Product, Risk, Operations; establish ownership, timelines, next steps, and customer communication; drive through resolution, RCA, and preventive actions
  • Meet contractual SLAs and internal commitments without exception — escalate early based on business impact, not SLA proximity
  • Communicate complex technical incidents to customer engineering teams and C-level stakeholders during live outages with clarity and composure
  • Ensure no critical issue is lost between teams — you are the single point of technical accountability

Proactive Account Health

  • Build and maintain a technical account plan for every assigned customer — understand their payment architecture, integrations, transaction flows, critical business journeys, and technical dependencies
  • Monitor account health continuously — analyze ticket trends, API error patterns, recurring issues, integration failures, reliability signals, and operational anomalies to identify risks before they escalate
  • Drive technical health reviews — present findings, remediation plans, owners, and deadlines; partner with CSM/Account teams to incorporate technical health into QBRs and account strategy
  • Prepare customers for launches, peak traffic events, migrations, and major releases — conduct readiness assessments and proactive capacity planning
  • Reduce repeat incidents over time — your success is measured by fewer avoidable escalations, not higher ticket volume

Technical Depth

  • Troubleshoot API integrations — webhook delivery failures, authentication issues, payment lifecycle anomalies, duplicate-event handling, idempotency violations, latency spikes, refund/settlement discrepancies, and dispute workflows
  • Interpret logs, trace transaction states — diagnose integration architecture issues, and guide customers through production vs. test environment differences
  • Translate technical root causes into executive-level business impact and remediation plans

What You Bring

Experience

  • 3–5+ years in Enterprise Technical Account Management, Technical Customer Success, Enterprise Support, Solutions Architecture, Customer Engineering, or similar customer-facing technical roles
  • Enterprise/global customer experience required — fintech/payments experience strongly preferred but not mandatory if you bring excellent API/SaaS experience
  • Track record of managing P1/P2 incidents at scale and driving cross-functional escalations in high-pressure environments
  • Strong API/integration understanding — REST APIs, webhooks, asynchronous event processing, error handling, integration patterns, and production reliability concepts

Capabilities

  • Executive communication — written and verbal English at a level suitable for C-level stakeholders during live incidents
  • Strong RCA and structured problem-solving capabilities
  • Cross-functional influence without authority — comfortable challenging Engineering, Product, or SRE constructively when customer outcomes are at risk
  • Ability to operate effectively across US and India time zones — comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience

What Great Looks Like

Extreme ownership • Customer obsession without being customer-controlled • Bias for action • Calm under pressure • Data-driven decision making • Ability to simplify complexity • Strong judgement—knows when to escalate and when to solve • Executive presence • Technical curiosity • Structured problem-solving • Ability to identify risks before they become escalations • Strong follow-through • Challenges respectfully; influences without friction

Success Measures

  • All Incident response and resolution SLA adherence
  • Escalation ageing and time-to-close performance
  • Repeat incident reduction and RCA completion quality
  • Customer technical health score improvement
  • Proactive risk identification rate (issues flagged before customer-impacting)
  • Preventive action closure within committed timelines
  • NPS satisfaction (NPS) on incident management and technical guidance
  • QBR/account-health readiness and stakeholder alignment
  • Reduction in recurring technical issues over time

  • Demonstrated ability to consistently meet or exceed revenue goals or targets   
  • Proven ability to understand customer needs, create and deliver customized, customer-focused pitches and solutions  
  • Effectively navigate through ambiguity and complexities related to client management

  • Solid knowledge of the search industry, trends, and customers needs

  • Collaborative teammate who can build successful team relationships with partners; and can prioritize multiple tasks  
  • Flexible and able to quickly adapt to changing business needs and processes  
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills  
  • Willingness to travel  
  • Arabic and English proficiency

Preferred  

  • Microsoft Ads Certification  
  • Experienced using Excel to analyse information, including data manipulation, V-Lookups, creating and using pivot tables, and data analysis
